Action_BusPublish.description: Publishes an event on the page's bus, which bindings listening to it receive at once.

name.description: The event's name; a binding can match only identifier names.

payload.description: What listeners receive as `$event`. It is delivered at once, to the bindings listening now.

sourceId.description:
The id the event is published under; it need not be a mounted block.

A binding listens to it as `$block.<sourceId>.event.<name>`.

Action_BusPublish.title: Publish an event

Action_Copy.description:
Copies text to the clipboard, optionally with a toast.

A failed write stops the chain.

notify.description: A toast after copying: `{ level: "info" | "success", title }`. The title is not an expression.

value.description: The text to copy — an expression; whatever it resolves to is copied as text.

Action_Copy.title: Copy to clipboard

Action_Delay.description:
Waits, then the chain continues.

Not a debounce: every event still runs its own delayed chain.

ms.description: How long to wait, in milliseconds (0–5000).

Action_Delay.title: Wait

Action_FormReset.description:
Restores a form to its baseline and clears its errors.

The baseline is the values it had when it mounted, or at its last successful `form.submit`. An unknown id does nothing.
Action_FormReset.title: Reset a form

Action_FormSubmit.description:
Sends a form's values to the Corezoid process or a sim-api method, then runs `onSuccess` or `onError`.

It does not validate — run `form.validate` and an `if` first. There is no double-submit guard, and the page's URL query is not sent. Response actions in the reply are applied before `onSuccess`.

formId.description: The `Form` node's id. Its `vm.<valueKey>` is sent as `formData`. Keys not declared in the form's `fields` are sent too; an unknown form sends `{}`.

onError.description:
Runs with `$error` when the call itself fails (network, access, Corezoid unreachable).

Without it, a failure stops the chain.

onSuccess.description:
Runs after the reply, with `$event` = the reply.

A Corezoid reply with a non-2xx `code` still lands here — branch on `$event.code`.

simapiMethod.description: The sim-api method to call; required with `via: "simapi"`.

via.description: `corezoid`: `page/submit` → the form's process `/send`. `simapi`: calls `simapiMethod` with `{ formData, …simapiExtraParams }`.

Action_FormSubmit.title: Submit a form

Action_FormValidate.description:
Checks a form's fields and writes its errors and validity to the view model.

It does not stop the chain when the form is invalid — gate the next step with `{ "type": "if", "cond": "vm.valid.<valueKey>", "then": [ … ] }`. An unknown form id counts as valid and writes nothing.

scope.description: Check only these field names. Default: every field the form declares, on screen or not.

setErrors.description:
Write the results (default `true`): `vm.errors.<valueKey>` and `vm.valid.<valueKey>`.

With `false` nothing observable happens.

Action_FormValidate.title: Validate a form

Action_If.description:
Runs `then` when the condition is truthy, otherwise `else`.

Both branches share the outer chain's `$result`; a failure inside one stops only that branch.

cond.description: The condition, bare or in `{{ }}`. An expression error counts as falsy.

then.description: The chain to run when the condition is truthy.

Action_If.title: Branch

Action_Log.description:
Writes a telemetry event (`renderer.action.log`) — for debugging a chain.

The runtime's console shows only `warn` and `error`.

level.description: How severe the entry is: `debug`, `info`, `warn` or `error`.

Action_Log.title: Write to the log

Action_NavigateLocal.description:
Opens another page of this Smart Form, an in-app path or an external URL.

A literal `to: ""` stays on the page and changes only the query. A value that resolves to nothing is skipped.

The `#b=` fragment is not carried over. On a production page, a bare page id whose page has exactly one route without parameters goes to that short URL.

history.description: `push` adds a history entry (default); `replace` replaces the current one.

prefetch.description:
`false` stops the host from preloading the target page on hover or focus. Default `true`.

Set it when the target's `/get` is not a cheap read.

query.description:
Replaces the URL query (no merge with the current one). Each value is an expression.

Objects are JSON-encoded, other values turned into text, empty ones dropped.

to.description:
A page id of this Smart Form, an in-app path starting with `/`, or an external `http(s)://` or `//` URL.

A literal `""` stays on the current page and changes only the query. A value that resolves to nothing — an expression that resolves to `""` included — is skipped (`renderer.navigate.noTarget`).

Action_NavigateLocal.title: Go to a page

Action_NavigateRoute.description:
Opens a route the Smart Form declares in its pages' `routes`, by name.

The host builds the short URL `/sf/{appKey}{path}` from the active release's route table. A refusal — an unknown name, a value that does not fit its parameter, a develop page with no route table — stops the chain.

blockRoutes.description: Block id → block-local state for the new page's `#b=` fragment. Each value is an expression.

history.description: `push` adds a history entry (default); `replace` replaces the current one.

name.description: A route name from the Smart Form's routes (`graph.layer`).

params.description: One expression per `:param` of the route; each must resolve to a string or a number. `null`, a boolean, an object or an array throws `route.invalidParamValue`.

query.description: The URL query, as on `navigate.local`. Each value is an expression.

Action_NavigateRoute.title: Go to a route

expireMs.description:
Milliseconds before the toast closes; `0` keeps it until closed.

Defaults by level: success 3000, info 5000, warn 7000, error 0.

helperText.description: A second line under the title.

title.description: The message. An expression; if it resolves to nothing, the template text is shown.

toastId.description: A test id for the toast. A second toast with the same id does not replace the first.

Action_OverlayClose.description: Closes the overlay with this `surface` and `id`.

id.description: The id the overlay was opened with.

intent.description: Accepted and currently unused — nothing reads it.

surface.description: The surface the overlay was opened on.

Action_OverlayClose.title: Close a modal or drawer

Action_OverlayOpen.description:
Opens an overlay and renders its `content` above the page.

The content shares the page's view model and bus but sees no loop variables — copy the row into `vm` first. For a dialog, make the content a `Modal` whose `onClose` runs `overlay.close`.

content.description: The node to render in the overlay. Without it nothing renders.

id.description: Names the overlay; opening the same key again replaces it.

surface.description: Part of the overlay's key (`surface` + `id`); it adds no chrome.

Action_OverlayOpen.title: Open a modal or drawer

Action_SimapiCall.description:
Calls a sim-api method; the reply goes to `$result.<assignTo>` for the rest of the chain.

sim-api checks the viewer's access. The reply is never applied as response actions, and there is no `onSuccess` — success is simply the next action.

assignTo.description:
Puts the reply in `$result.<name>` for the rest of this chain — not in the view model.

To keep it, follow with a `state` action: `"value": "{{ $result.regions }}"`.

method.description: The sim-api JSON-RPC method (`actor/list`). `page/submit` gets the page's coordinates from the runtime.

onError.description:
Runs with `$error` when the call fails; then the outer chain continues.

Without it, a failure stops the chain.

Action_SimapiCall.title: Call sim-api

Action_State.description:
Writes a value into the view model, or merges an object into it.

`mode: "set"` writes `value` at `path`; `mode: "merge"` shallow-merges `patch` into the object at `path`.

mode.description: `set` writes one value; `merge` shallow-merges an object.

patch.description:
The object to merge (`merge` only, and required there).

Shallow: one level deep. A missing or non-object target counts as `{}`.

path.description:
Where to write: dots or brackets (`rows[0].name`), or a JSON Pointer (`/rows/0/name`).

A leading `vm.` is allowed. `""`, `"/"` and `"vm"` mean the whole view model.

value.description:
The value to write (`set` only, and required there).

Missing parents are created — an array when the next segment is a number. At the root it replaces the whole view model.

Action_State.title: Write to the view model

Action_ThemeSet.description:
Switches the page to another of the form's themes.

Applied only if the form lists the theme in `themes.switchable`; the runtime remembers the viewer's choice for this form.

theme.description: A theme id, or an expression resolving to one (`{{ $event.value }}`). Ignored unless it resolves to a non-empty string.

Action_ThemeSet.title: Switch theme

Action_WidgetCall.description: Calls one of a block's `api` methods; its return value goes to `$result.<assignTo>`.

args.description: Passed to the method as is; not checked against its declared args.

assignTo.description: Puts the method's return value in `$result.<name>` for the rest of this chain.

method.description: One of the block's `api` methods (see the block's reference).

target.description: The node id of a block on this page.

timeoutMs.description:
How long to wait for a method that returns a promise (default 10000); running out stops the chain.

An unknown target or method throws in development and does nothing in production.

Action_WidgetCall.title: Call a block

ClientAction.description: One step of an action chain — a closed set of 17 action types, keyed on `type`.

Definition.description: Reusable subtree referenced by $ref. Stored at <app-root>/definitions/<name>.

Expression.description: Either a literal string, or a string containing one or more {{ JSONata }} expressions. Reactively re-evaluated on render.

JsonPatchOp.description: RFC 6902 operation with the renderer's supported `op` subset.

Locale.description: i18n dictionary. BCP 47 language tag → flat key → string.

PageBinding.description: When a block emits an event, run an action chain.

do.description:
The chain to run, with `$event` = the event's payload and a fresh `$result`.

Every emission runs its own chain.

on.description:
The event this rule listens to: `$block.<blockId>.event.<eventName>`, written without `{{ }}`.

Both parts are identifiers, so a block inside a `for` (id `<id>:<key>`) cannot be targeted.

when.description:
Optional guard: the chain runs only when it is truthy.

Bare or in `{{ }}`. It sees `vm`, `$event` (the payload) and the host variables — not `$block` state and no loop variables.

RAction_Assign.description:
Sets one value in the view model.

Same paths as `state`; missing parents are created; `""`, `"/"` or `"vm"` replaces the whole view model.

path.description: Where to write: `status`, `vm.status` and `/status` are the same.

value.description: The value to write, as sent.

RAction_Assign.title: Set a view-model value

RAction_Navigate.description: Opens a page, an in-app path or an external URL — the same routing as `navigate.local`.

history.description: `push` adds a history entry (default); `replace` replaces the current one.

query.description: The URL query; every value must be a string.

to.description: A page id of this Smart Form, an in-app path starting with `/`, or an external URL.

RAction_Navigate.title: Go to a page

RAction_Notify.description: Shows a toast, like the client `notify` — but every value, title and helper text included, is shown as sent.
RAction_Notify.title: Show a toast

RAction_Patch.description:
Applies a JSON Patch to the rendered tree or to the view model — atomically.

If any op fails, none is applied (telemetry `renderer.patch.rollback`) and the next action still runs.

ops.description: The JSON Patch operations, at least one. Paths are JSON Pointers (`/rows/0/name`). For `tree` they start at the root node (`/props/title`, `/children/0/props/text`), for `vm` at the view model.

RAction_Patch.title: Patch the tree or view model

RAction_Redirect.description: Leaves the app for an absolute `http(s)` URL.

history.description: Accepted; the runtime always opens the URL as a new navigation (`location.assign`).

url.description: The URL; it must start with `http://` or `https://`.

RAction_Redirect.title: Leave the app

RAction_VmMerge.description:
Deep-merges an object into the view model.

Nested objects merge key by key; arrays, scalars and `null` replace; no key is ever removed.

patch.description: The object to merge into the view model.

RAction_VmMerge.title: Merge into the view model

ResponseAction.description:
What a `form.submit` reply may ask the page to do — a closed set of six types, applied in order.

They come from the Corezoid process's `/send` reply (`data.actions`) or a `via: "simapi"` method's result, and are applied exactly as sent: no expressions. Realtime frames never carry them.

name.description: Namespaced route name, unique within the Smart Form (e.g. graph.layer).

params.description: One declaration per :param of path, keyed by parameter name.

path.description: Pattern relative to /sf/{appKey}: '/' or '/'-separated lowercase-slug literals and :param segments, no trailing '/'.

actor.description: Only with type slug: the slug is the actors.ref of an actor of this form; the runtime resolves it to $route.ids.<param>.

allOf.comment: id is required for any node that participates in registry/bus (i.e. type set).

TreeNode.description:
One UI node: a component `type` with its `props`, `children` and event `actions`.

A node can also carry `if` / `visibility` conditions, a `for` loop, or be a `$ref` to a definition.

$ref.description:
Replaces this node with a reusable subtree from `definitions/<name>`.

The server inlines it before the page renders.

actions.description:
Event name (`onClick`) → the action chain it runs.

Only the events the component declares are wired. Inside the chain `$event` is what the component passed.

children.description: Child nodes: a list, or named slots when the component declares them.

oneOf.description: Named-slot children, when the parent declares editor.slots.

for.description:
Renders this node once per item of an array.

`items` produces the array, `as` names the item (`$<as>`), `keyBy` picks the key field and `indexAs` names the position. Loop variables are visible in this node and its subtree only.

as.description: The name of the current item: `as: "row"` makes it `$row` in this node and its subtree.

indexAs.description: Optional name for the item's 0-based position (`indexAs: "i"` → `$i`).

items.description: JSONata expression (bare or wrapped in {{ }}) returning an array; a non-array renders no copies.

keyBy.description: The item field used as each copy's key. Without it the key is the item's `id`, and failing that its position.

id.description:
The node's id: what `widget.call`, `$block.<id>` and bindings address.

A plain identifier, never an expression. Inside a `for` the renderer renames each copy `<id>:<key>`, so a block in a loop cannot be targeted by a binding.

if.description:
Mounts the node only while this condition is truthy.

JSONata, bare or in `{{ }}`. When falsy the node and its subtree are not mounted at all — use `visibility: "hidden"` to keep their state.

props.description:
The component's props. Any value may be a `{{ }}` expression.

Validated against the type's contract when the page is saved, not when it renders.

slot.description: Which named slot of the parent this node goes into.

type.description:
The component this node renders — one of the catalog types.

An unknown type renders the renderer's fallback and is refused by sim-api at save.

variant.description: A variant name for the component, when its contract defines one.

anyOf.description: JSONata expression, bare or wrapped in {{ }}, resolving to one of the enum values; any other result renders as visible. 'hidden' keeps the node mounted.

visibility.description:
Shows, hides or disables the node: `visible`, `hidden`, `disabled`, or an expression resolving to one.

Bare or in `{{ }}`, like `if`. The three literals stay literals; any other result is `visible`. `hidden` keeps the node mounted (its state survives the toggle); `if` unmounts it.

ViewModel.description: Initial mutable data store. Shape is page-specific.

pageSchema.description: Normative JSON Schema for stored page configs (a Smart Form file pages/<pageId>/config, authored as JSON). sim-api validates every saved file whose JSON has schemaVersion and tree against it, then each node's props against cdu-catalog.schema.json.

bindings.description:
Page-level rules: when a block emits an event, run an action chain.

Each rule is `{ on, when?, do }`. A primitive wires its own events in its `actions`; a binding is how the page reacts to a block.

description.description: A note about the page for its authors. It is stored but never sent to the page.

id.description: Page id. Keep it equal to the containing folder name (not enforced); page/render returns it as pageId.

meta.description:
Settings for how the page is served and for tooling — not part of what it shows.

`initViaCorezoid`, `vmKeys` and `routeState` change what `page/render` returns; `tags`, `author` and `deprecated` are for tooling only.

author.description: Who maintains the page. For tooling; not sent to the page.

deprecated.description: Marks the page as deprecated for tooling. Not sent to the page.

initViaCorezoid.description:
`true` makes `page/render` call the form's Corezoid process (`/get`) to seed the view model.

Without it the page starts from the `viewModel` file alone.

routeState.description: View-model keys the host mirrors into the URL so they survive reload/back-forward and can be shared as a link. Dot paths; the initial viewModel value is the default and is omitted from the URL. Only string/number/boolean values travel. Echoed by page/render as routeState.

tags.description: Free-form labels for tooling. Not sent to the page.

vmKeys.description: Optional allowlist of top-level view-model keys page/render keeps. Omitted = no filtering; a present array (including []) drops every other key, so [] ships an empty view model.

routes.description:
Short URLs that open this page: `/sf/{appKey}{path}`.

Optional. Names must be unique and patterns must not overlap across the pages of a Smart Form; sim-api checks the whole table when a release is published and reports `route.*` codes.

schemaVersion.description: Major.Minor. Author '2.0'. page/render echoes it; nothing checks or migrates it.

title.description: The page title, sent to the host by `page/render` when it is not empty.

tree.description: The root node of the page — everything the page shows grows from it.

pageSchema.title: SimulatorPageConfig

action:navigate.local.title: Go to a page
action:navigate.local.summary: Opens another page of this Smart Form, an in-app path or an external URL.
action:navigate.local.body:
A literal `to: ""` stays on the page and changes only the query. A value that resolves to nothing is skipped.

The `#b=` fragment is not carried over. On a production page, a bare page id whose page has exactly one route without parameters goes to that short URL.

action:navigate.local.history.summary: `push` adds a history entry (default); `replace` replaces the current one.

action:navigate.local.prefetch.summary: `false` stops the host from preloading the target page on hover or focus. Default `true`.
action:navigate.local.prefetch.body: Set it when the target's `/get` is not a cheap read.

action:navigate.local.query.summary: Replaces the URL query (no merge with the current one). Each value is an expression.
action:navigate.local.query.body: Objects are JSON-encoded, other values turned into text, empty ones dropped.

action:navigate.local.to.summary: A page id of this Smart Form, an in-app path starting with `/`, or an external `http(s)://` or `//` URL.
action:navigate.local.to.body: A literal `""` stays on the current page and changes only the query. A value that resolves to nothing — an expression that resolves to `""` included — is skipped (`renderer.navigate.noTarget`).

action:navigate.route.title: Go to a route
action:navigate.route.summary: Opens a route the Smart Form declares in its pages' `routes`, by name.
action:navigate.route.body: The host builds the short URL `/sf/{appKey}{path}` from the active release's route table. A refusal — an unknown name, a value that does not fit its parameter, a develop page with no route table — stops the chain.

action:navigate.route.blockRoutes.summary: Block id → block-local state for the new page's `#b=` fragment. Each value is an expression.

action:navigate.route.history.summary: `push` adds a history entry (default); `replace` replaces the current one.

action:navigate.route.name.summary: A route name from the Smart Form's routes (`graph.layer`).

action:navigate.route.params.summary: One expression per `:param` of the route; each must resolve to a string or a number. `null`, a boolean, an object or an array throws `route.invalidParamValue`.

action:navigate.route.query.summary: The URL query, as on `navigate.local`. Each value is an expression.

action:notify.expireMs.summary: Milliseconds before the toast closes; `0` keeps it until closed.
action:notify.expireMs.body: Defaults by level: success 3000, info 5000, warn 7000, error 0.

action:notify.helperText.summary: A second line under the title.

action:notify.title.summary: The message. An expression; if it resolves to nothing, the template text is shown.

action:notify.toastId.summary: A test id for the toast. A second toast with the same id does not replace the first.

action:overlay.close.title: Close a modal or drawer
action:overlay.close.summary: Closes the overlay with this `surface` and `id`.

action:overlay.close.id.summary: The id the overlay was opened with.

action:overlay.close.intent.summary: Accepted and currently unused — nothing reads it.

action:overlay.close.surface.summary: The surface the overlay was opened on.

action:overlay.open.title: Open a modal or drawer
action:overlay.open.summary: Opens an overlay and renders its `content` above the page.
action:overlay.open.body: The content shares the page's view model and bus but sees no loop variables — copy the row into `vm` first. For a dialog, make the content a `Modal` whose `onClose` runs `overlay.close`.

action:overlay.open.content.summary: The node to render in the overlay. Without it nothing renders.

action:overlay.open.id.summary: Names the overlay; opening the same key again replaces it.

action:overlay.open.surface.summary: Part of the overlay's key (`surface` + `id`); it adds no chrome.

action:simapi.call.title: Call sim-api
action:simapi.call.summary: Calls a sim-api method; the reply goes to `$result.<assignTo>` for the rest of the chain.
action:simapi.call.body: sim-api checks the viewer's access. The reply is never applied as response actions, and there is no `onSuccess` — success is simply the next action.

action:simapi.call.assignTo.summary: Puts the reply in `$result.<name>` for the rest of this chain — not in the view model.
action:simapi.call.assignTo.body: To keep it, follow with a `state` action: `"value": "{{ $result.regions }}"`.

action:simapi.call.method.summary: The sim-api JSON-RPC method (`actor/list`). `page/submit` gets the page's coordinates from the runtime.

action:simapi.call.onError.summary: Runs with `$error` when the call fails; then the outer chain continues.
action:simapi.call.onError.body: Without it, a failure stops the chain.

action:state.title: Write to the view model
action:state.summary: Writes a value into the view model, or merges an object into it.
action:state.body: `mode: "set"` writes `value` at `path`; `mode: "merge"` shallow-merges `patch` into the object at `path`.

action:state.mode.summary: `set` writes one value; `merge` shallow-merges an object.

action:state.patch.summary: The object to merge (`merge` only, and required there).
action:state.patch.body: Shallow: one level deep. A missing or non-object target counts as `{}`.

action:state.path.summary: Where to write: dots or brackets (`rows[0].name`), or a JSON Pointer (`/rows/0/name`).
action:state.path.body: A leading `vm.` is allowed. `""`, `"/"` and `"vm"` mean the whole view model.

action:state.value.summary: The value to write (`set` only, and required there).
action:state.value.body: Missing parents are created — an array when the next segment is a number. At the root it replaces the whole view model.

action:theme.set.title: Switch theme
action:theme.set.summary: Switches the page to another of the form's themes.
action:theme.set.body: Applied only if the form lists the theme in `themes.switchable`; the runtime remembers the viewer's choice for this form.

action:theme.set.theme.summary: A theme id, or an expression resolving to one (`{{ $event.value }}`). Ignored unless it resolves to a non-empty string.

action:widget.call.title: Call a block
action:widget.call.summary: Calls one of a block's `api` methods; its return value goes to `$result.<assignTo>`.

action:widget.call.args.summary: Passed to the method as is; not checked against its declared args.

action:widget.call.assignTo.summary: Puts the method's return value in `$result.<name>` for the rest of this chain.

action:widget.call.method.summary: One of the block's `api` methods (see the block's reference).

action:widget.call.target.summary: The node id of a block on this page.

action:widget.call.timeoutMs.summary: How long to wait for a method that returns a promise (default 10000); running out stops the chain.
action:widget.call.timeoutMs.body: An unknown target or method throws in development and does nothing in production.

api:AccountDetails.close.summary: Unmount the panel. The next `open` starts fresh, on the side `accountType` names.

api:AccountDetails.open.summary: Mount the panel. In `modal` presentation this is what shows the dialog.

api:AccountDetails.refresh.summary: Re-read the pair. A no-op while the panel is closed: nothing is mounted to re-read.

api:AccountDetails.setAccountType.summary: Show the other side. A no-op while the panel is closed (the next `open` starts on the `accountType` prop), and for a side the read has shown the pair does not have. Called before the pair is read, it is kept; should that side turn out missing, the panel shows the other.

api:AccountTemplate.addSection.summary: Appends a new section with one field and selects it. Does nothing when read-only.

api:AccountTemplate.reset.summary: Discards the unsaved changes and the undo history, returning to the last saved template, and drops the access and accounts tabs' staged changes.
api:AccountTemplate.reset.body: The template itself is untouched when read-only.

api:AccountTemplate.save.summary: Saves the template, creating it when it is new; `saved` fires on success.
api:AccountTemplate.save.body:
Does nothing when read-only. With blocking issues it saves nothing and opens the problem list.
A new template is created together with the access and accounts staged on its tabs (all or
nothing); on an existing one those tabs save with their own button.

api:AccountTemplate.setTab.summary: Opens the `constructor` (Form fields), `preview`, `accounts`, `hierarchy` or `access` tab; for `access`, `accessScope` picks the template's or its actors' access (default: the current one).

api:AccountTemplatesList.search.summary: Replace the search query. Resets to page 1.

api:AccountTemplatesList.setFilter.summary: Patch the filter (omitted keys keep their value) and optionally switch tab. Resets to page 1.

api:ActorFilterEditor.openCreate.summary: Open the editor on a new filter.

api:ActorFilterEditor.openEdit.summary: Open the editor on a saved filter.

api:ActorList.open.summary: Open an actor in the list's own detail, as a row click (`drilled: false`, beside the list) or a double click (`drilled: true`, instead of it) would — past the open actor's unsaved-changes guard, and into the block route like any opening. For a page that learns of an actor elsewhere (a create flow, a search) and wants it shown here. Nothing opens while both row actions are `event`.

api:ActorView.requestLeave.summary: Asks the block whether the page may leave it, before the host navigates away or unmounts it.
api:ActorView.requestLeave.body:
The answer arrives as `leaveResolved` with the same `requestId`. When there are unsaved
changes the user may first be asked whether to discard them; a request made while another is
still waiting for the user is answered `false`.

api:ChangeJournal.loadMore.summary: Append the next page, if there is one.

api:ChangeJournal.refresh.summary: Re-read the current window from the server.

api:ChangeJournal.setFilter.summary: Patch the filter; omitted keys keep their current value.

api:Chart.copyImage.summary: Copy the chart's image to the clipboard, as the menu's «Copy image» does, and tell the viewer how it went. Resolves `true` once copied, `false` when there was no image or the browser refused the write — a page can branch on it, e.g. to offer «Export to PNG» instead.

api:Chart.downloadCsv.summary: Download the chart's data as `<title>.csv`, as the menu's «Export to CSV» does.

api:Chart.downloadPng.summary: Download the chart as `<title>.png`, as the menu's «Export to PNG» does, telling the viewer if it cannot.

api:Chart.exportCsv.summary: The rendered chart as CSV text — one row per point, one column per series — or `null` with no data.

api:Chart.exportPng.summary: Export the current canvas chart. Table/KPI renderers return `null`.

api:Chart.openTransactions.summary: Open the transactions behind a metric, as a click on it would — typically one a `metricClick` handler received. Returns `false` when nothing opens: `drillDown` is `none`, or the metric is an aggregate or names no account.

api:Chart.refresh.summary: Refetch configuration and visible dashboard data.

api:ColorPalette.select.summary: Choose a colour; omit `color` to clear the choice.

api:CreateAccount.close.summary: Close the dialog without creating anything.

api:CreateActor.close.summary: Close the panel without creating anything.

api:CreateActor.reset.summary: Clears the draft back to an empty one, keeping the current template.

api:CreateActor.submit.summary: Programmatic Save — validates first, exactly like clicking the button.

api:CreateEvent.close.summary: Hides the form and drops the draft, as Cancel does, and fires `closed`.

api:CreateEvent.open.summary: Shows the event form. The block renders nothing until this is called.

api:CreateEvent.reset.summary: Restores the opening draft and clears validation messages, leaving the form open.
api:CreateEvent.reset.body: In create mode that is an empty event; in edit mode, the event as last loaded.

api:CreateEvent.submit.summary: Validates first, exactly like clicking the Save button.

api:CreateSmartForm.close.summary: Close the dialog. An install already queued still runs to the end.

api:CreateTransaction.close.summary: Unmount the form, dropping the draft — the next `open` starts fresh.

api:CreateTransaction.open.summary: Mount the form. In `modal` presentation this is what shows the dialog.

api:CreateTransaction.submit.body:
Fire-and-forget, like every CDU action: a bus api method returns synchronously, and a
submit is asynchronous by nature. The OUTCOME arrives as an event —
`transactionCreated` / `transferCreated` on success, `submitFailed` otherwise — which
is the channel a page binds its own follow-up actions to.

api:CreateTransaction.switchMode.summary: Show the other mode. Switching keeps the account, amount and comment.

api:DashboardWizard.openCreate.summary: Open the wizard for a new chart.

api:DashboardWizard.openEdit.summary: Open the wizard to edit an existing chart actor.

api:ESign.reset.summary: Clears the current attempt back to `idle`. A signature is permanent and stays.

api:ESign.startSign.summary: Prepares the document and opens the signing widget; does nothing unless the user may sign now.

api:EventsCalendar.goTo.summary: Jump to the period containing `date` (unix seconds).

api:EventsCalendar.refresh.summary: Re-read the calendar — a neighbouring block changed an event (same-tab writes bring no realtime frame).

api:EventsList.open.summary: Open an event in the list's own detail — beside the list or drilled into (`drilled`; by default the list's own click action: beside for the chat list, drilled for the feed) — past the open one's unsaved-changes guard and into the block route, as a click would. For a page that learns of a changed event elsewhere. Emits nothing, like `select`. A no-op under `rowClickAction: 'event'`.

api:EventsList.readAll.summary: With `streams`: mark a stream (the picked one by default) and its sub-streams read; their counts drop to zero.

api:EventsList.refresh.summary: Re-read the list — a neighbouring block changed an event this list holds a copy of (a chat renamed, a message sent: its title, last activity and place in the order). Same-tab writes bring no realtime frame (the own-echo filter drops them), so the page relays them here.

api:EventsList.select.summary: Paint a row as selected — a host or a neighbouring block opened that chat. Emits nothing: a command is not a pick, and echoing it as `eventSelected` would loop a page that binds one to the other.

api:EventsList.setStream.summary: With `streams`: pick a stream on the bar, as a click would — and announce it (`streamChanged`).

api:GraphEditor.focusActor.summary: Open a layer, select one actor on it and centre the camera.

api:GraphEditor.openLayer.summary: Open another layer. Writes the block-local route, so it survives a reload.

api:ImportExport.close.summary: Drop back to neither side chosen, closing whatever dialog that side had open.

api:ImportExport.openExport.summary: Show the Export tab. With `actors` / `forms`, those are added to the export QUEUE first — the same door the Graphs and Templates lists use. There is no ad-hoc export dialog.

api:ImportExport.openImport.summary: Show the Import tab, whose drop zone is the import entry point.

api:NotificationCenter.markRead.summary: Mark entries read — exactly one of `ids`, `actorId`, `all`. Emits `allRead` for `all`.

api:NotificationCenter.refresh.summary: Re-read the feed and the counts.

api:SearchEntity.focus.summary: Focus the field (a kit combobox opens on focus).

api:SearchEntity.search.summary: Open the panel with a query prefilled, as if the user had typed it.

api:SelectAccount.select.summary: Select / restore a pair by ids (names hydrate via `*_get`).

api:SelectActor.setScope.summary: Change the template scope; omit `formId` for the whole workspace.

api:SelectActorAccount.select.summary: Select (or restore) a pair by ids. Resolved against the actor's OWN accounts, so ids the actor does not hold are a no-op — that is the block's whole point, and a stub would publish a pair with blank names that no `*_get` here can complete. A pair the field itself shows as disabled (`disableSystemAccounts`) is refused too: the api may not commit what a person is forbidden to pick.

api:SelectActorField.select.summary: Select (or restore) a field by its key. Resolved against the actor's OWN fields, so a key its forms do not hold is a no-op rather than a field with no title.

api:SelectUser.focus.summary: Focus the field (opens the panel — a kit combobox opens on focus).

api:SelectUser.search.summary: Open the panel with a query prefilled, as if the user had typed it.

api:SelectUser.setValue.summary: Set the selection imperatively, without a pick.

api:SmartFormEditor.insertNode.summary: Inserts a new component of `type` into node `parentId` at `index`, with its default props, and selects it.
api:SmartFormEditor.insertNode.body:
Applies to the page shown in the structure. Does nothing when the editor is read-only or the
type or parent node is unknown.

api:SmartFormEditor.openFile.summary: Opens the file whose id is `fileId`. Does nothing when the form has no such file.

api:SmartFormEditor.openPage.summary: Opens the config of page `pageId` and fires `pageOpened`. Does nothing for a page the form does not have.

api:SmartFormEditor.publish.summary: Asks the user to confirm publishing `develop` to `production`; it does not publish by itself.
api:SmartFormEditor.publish.body:
Once the user confirms, unsaved edits are saved, a release is created and `published` fires.
Does nothing when the user cannot modify the form or it lacks either environment.

api:SmartFormEditor.redo.summary: Redoes the last undone edit of the open file. Does nothing when `canRedo` is `false`.

api:SmartFormEditor.revert.summary: Discards the unsaved edits of every file, returning each to its last saved text.

api:SmartFormEditor.save.summary: Saves every unsaved file that passes validation now, without waiting for autosave.
api:SmartFormEditor.save.body: A file with blocking issues stays unsaved. `saved` fires with the ids of the files written.

api:SmartFormEditor.selectNode.summary: Selects node `nodeId` of the page in the structure, scrolls to it and brings the Inspector forward.
api:SmartFormEditor.selectNode.body: The JSON source stays in front when it is the current workspace. `selectionChanged` fires.

api:SmartFormEditor.setMode.summary: Sets how a page's tab shows: `code` (source), `split` (source + preview) or `preview`.

api:SmartFormEditor.setPanel.summary: Brings a tool window forward: `inspector` or `ai` as the workspace, the `theme` tab, or `history` at the bottom.

api:SmartFormEditor.setPreviewVisible.summary: Shows or hides the live preview: `true` switches to `split` (`preview` on a narrow editor), `false` to `code`.

api:SmartFormEditor.setSurface.body:
`ai` falls back to `inspector` when `aiConsole` is `false`; a tab showing only the preview
returns to its source.

api:SmartFormEditor.setView.summary: Switches the workspace by `view`: `json` shows the JSON source, `outline` the Inspector with the Outline open.

api:SmartFormEditor.undo.summary: Undoes the last edit of the open file. Does nothing when `canUndo` is `false`.

api:Streams.readAll.summary: Mark a stream (the picked one by default) and its sub-streams read; their counts drop to zero.

api:Streams.setStream.summary: Pick a stream, as a click would — and announce it (`streamChanged`), so a bound list follows.

api:TransactionView.open.summary: Show another transaction; `createdAt` (ms) is its partition hint.

api:TransactionsList.refresh.summary: Re-read the current page from the server.

api:TransactionsList.selectRow.summary: Programmatically select a row, as if it were clicked — fires `transactionSelected`.

api:TransactionsList.setFilter.summary: Patch the filter; omitted keys keep their current value. Resets to page 1.

api:Webhooks.openCreate.summary: Open the create dialog (a no-op for a viewer without SETTINGS_MANAGEMENT).

api:WorkspaceSwitcher.select.summary: Switch to a workspace by accId.

binding:do.summary: The chain to run, with `$event` = the event's payload and a fresh `$result`.
binding:do.body: Every emission runs its own chain.

binding:on.summary: The event this rule listens to: `$block.<blockId>.event.<eventName>`, written without `{{ }}`.
binding:on.body: Both parts are identifiers, so a block inside a `for` (id `<id>:<key>`) cannot be targeted.

binding:when.summary: Optional guard: the chain runs only when it is truthy.
binding:when.body: Bare or in `{{ }}`. It sees `vm`, `$event` (the payload) and the host variables — not `$block` state and no loop variables.

concept:action-chain.title: Action chain
concept:action-chain.summary: The list of client actions an event runs, in order, each one waiting for the one before.
concept:action-chain.body:
A step that fails stops the rest of the chain — unless it is a `simapi.call` or `form.submit` with
its own `onError` branch, which runs instead. A step whose arguments do not match its schema is
skipped, and the chain goes on.

concept:binding.title: Binding
concept:binding.summary: A page-level rule: when a block emits an event, run an action chain.
concept:binding.body:
`on` names the event (`$block.<id>.event.<name>`), the optional `when` filters it, and `do` is the
chain. A primitive wires its events in its own `actions` instead; a binding is how a page reacts to
a block it cannot otherwise reach into.

concept:definition.title: Definition
concept:definition.summary: A reusable subtree stored in `definitions/<name>`, used by a node with `$ref: "#/definitions/<name>"`.
concept:definition.body: The server inlines it before the page renders, so a definition costs nothing at runtime.

concept:expression.title: Expression
concept:expression.summary: A JSONata expression in `{{ }}` that computes a prop value from the page's data when the page renders.
concept:expression.body:
A string that is exactly one `{{ … }}` takes the expression's own type — a number stays a number. A
string with text around it interpolates each part into text. `if`, `visibility`, `for.items` and a
binding's `when` are expressions already, so there the braces are optional.

An expression cannot change anything: it has no side effects, and an error or a timeout yields an
empty value instead of breaking the page.

concept:form.title: Form
concept:form.summary: A `Form` node keeps its fields' values in `vm.<valueKey>`; `form.*` actions validate, submit and reset it.
concept:form.body:
`form.validate` writes `vm.errors.<valueKey>` and `vm.valid.<valueKey>`; `form.submit` sends a copy
of `vm.<valueKey>` and does not validate on its own.

concept:loop.title: Loop (`for`)
concept:loop.summary: A node with `for` renders once per item of an array, each copy seeing its item as `$<as>`.
concept:loop.body:
`items` must produce an array — anything else renders no copies. Copies are keyed by `keyBy`, the
item's `id` or its position, and a node inside is renamed `<id>:<key>`.

concept:overlay.title: Overlay
concept:overlay.summary: A modal or drawer opened by `overlay.open`, keyed by `surface` + `id`, rendered above the page.
concept:overlay.body:
Its `content` shares the page's view model and bus but sees no loop variables, so a row action
copies the row into `vm` before it opens the overlay.

concept:page.title: Anatomy of a Smart Form
concept:page.summary: A Smart Form is a set of pages; each page is a tree of nodes over its own data, wired by actions.
concept:page.body:
```text
Smart Form
├─ config · viewModel · locale     app-wide: shared data and texts
├─ theme                           tokens, the themes a viewer may switch
├─ definitions/<name>              subtrees a node uses through $ref
└─ pages/<page>
   ├─ config      tree (nodes: type · props · children · actions · if · for)
   │              bindings (block event → chain) · routes · meta.routeState
   ├─ viewModel   the data {{ vm.* }} reads
   └─ locale      the texts {{ $locale.* }} reads

render   page/render → config + viewModel + locale → renderer
act      event → client actions (state, simapi.call, form.submit, …)
reply    form.submit → response actions (patch, vm.merge, navigate, …)
```

Select a node to read about its component here; search for an action, a context or a concept.

concept:response-action.title: Response action
concept:response-action.summary: What a `form.submit` reply may ask the page to do: one of six actions, applied in order, exactly as sent.
concept:response-action.body:
They come from the Corezoid process's `/send` reply (`{ "code": 200, "data": { "actions": [ … ] } }`)
or from the result of a `via: "simapi"` method. A `simapi.call` reply is never applied as actions,
and realtime frames carry none. Then `form.submit.onSuccess` runs. Put a `navigate` last: view-model
writes after it land on the page being left.

concept:route-state.title: Route state
concept:route-state.summary: View-model keys the host mirrors into the URL, so a reload, back/forward or a shared link restores them.
concept:route-state.body: Declare them in `meta.routeState`; a page reads them as ordinary `vm` keys.

ctx:$\u003cas\u003e.title: Loop item
ctx:$\u003cas\u003e.summary: The current item inside a `for` directive, under the name its `as` gives (`as: "row"` → `$row`).
ctx:$\u003cas\u003e.body: `indexAs` adds the item's position under a second name.

ctx:$block.summary: Another block on the page, by its node `id`: `$block.<id>.state.<key>` reads its public state.
ctx:$block.body:
`$block.<id>.event.<name>` names one of its events — the form a binding's `on` uses. A block id may
contain hyphens; the renderer quotes them for you.

ctx:$error.summary: What failed, inside an `onError` chain — usually a sim-api error.

ctx:$event.summary: The payload of the event being handled — inside an action chain, a binding's `when` and its `do`.
ctx:$event.body:
For a primitive's action it is the first argument the component passes (`TextInput` / `Select`
`onChange`: `{ value }`); in a binding, the bus event's payload; in `form.submit.onSuccess`, the
submit reply `{ code, data, actions }`.

ctx:$form.summary: Reserved — always `{}` today. Read a form's values from `vm.<valueKey>`.

ctx:$locale.summary: The page dictionary for the active language: `$locale.<key>`.

ctx:$now.summary: The current time as an ISO 8601 string, refreshed on every evaluation.

ctx:$params.summary: The short-URL route parameters — the same object as `$route.params`, empty on a technical URL.
ctx:$params.body: `int` parameters are numbers; `slug` and `uuid` parameters are strings.

ctx:$query.summary: The URL query of the page on screen, as strings: `$query.<key>`.
ctx:$query.body: The last value wins for a repeated key; `jwt` and `tmpsid` are removed. `{}` when there is none.

ctx:$result.summary: This chain's results: `$result.<name>` for every earlier `simapi.call` / `widget.call` with `assignTo`.
ctx:$result.body:
The last `form.submit` reply is there too, under `` $result.`$submit` ``. Results live only until the
chain ends; to keep one, write it to the view model with a `state` action.

ctx:$route.summary: How the page was opened: `{ kind: 'direct', params: {} }` for a technical URL, or `{ kind: 'dynamic', name, params }` for a short `/sf/…` URL.

ctx:$theme.summary: The polarity of the theme the page shows: `light` or `dark`.

ctx:$themeId.summary: The id of the active theme: `light`, `dark`, `darcula` or a theme the form defines.

ctx:$themes.summary: The theme ids the viewer may switch to (`themes.switchable`) — the options of a `theme.set` picker.

ctx:$user.summary: The signed-in user — `id`, `login`, `nick` and, when set, `photo`; absent for a guest.
ctx:$user.body:
There are no roles or permissions here: gate the UI on data your process puts in the view model —
the API enforces access, not the UI.

ctx:vm.title: View model
ctx:vm.summary: The page's data: what `page/render` returned in `viewModel`, plus every later `state` write and backend patch.
ctx:vm.body:
Read it as `vm.<path>` (`{{ vm.order.total }}`). A path that does not exist evaluates to nothing, so
a bound prop falls back to its default rather than failing.

event:AccountDetails.accountTypeChanged.summary: Fired whenever the side changes, including via `setAccountType`.

event:AccountDetails.closed.summary: The panel asked its host to close — the modal's X or Esc, or the `close` api.

event:AccountDetails.formulaSaved.summary: A formula was saved or removed in the editor the panel opened; the panel has already re-read the pair.

event:AccountDetails.loaded.summary: Fired each time the pair is read: on open, on a change of side, on `refresh`.

event:AccountTemplate.back.summary: The native return button was activated.

event:AccountTemplate.closeRequested.summary: Reserved for a close request carrying `dirty`; the block does not fire it at present.
event:AccountTemplate.closeRequested.body: A page binding to it today receives nothing.

event:AccountTemplate.dirtyChanged.summary: Fires when the template gains or loses unsaved changes; `dirty` is the new value.

event:AccountTemplate.saved.summary: Fires when the template is saved; `formId` is its id, new for a template just created. On a system template, whose only editable part is its actors' access, a saved share of that access fires it too, so a page closes the editor the same way.

event:AccountTemplate.templateOpened.summary: Fires when the block switched to another template from the Hierarchy tab — `formId` is the one now open, absent for a new template being created under a parent.
event:AccountTemplate.templateOpened.body:
The block navigates by itself (asking first to discard unsaved changes); bind this to follow
it, e.g. into the page's route. The `formId` state follows too.

event:AccountTemplate.validityChanged.summary: Fires when the validation result changes; carries `valid` and `issueCount`.

event:AccountTemplatesList.exportQueueOp.summary: «Open» was pressed on «Added to the export queue» (with `exportQueueLink`): show the queue. Last, so a binding added in an editor still starts on the block's primary event.

event:AccountTemplatesList.formCreated.summary: A template was saved from the list's «Create Account Template».

event:AccountTemplatesList.formSelected.summary: A row was clicked — legacy opened the form's editor; bind this to open one.

event:ActorAccounts.accessChanged.summary: «Manage access» saved a change to a pair's access rules.

event:ActorAccounts.accountCreated.summary: The embedded dialog created an account on the actor.

event:ActorAccounts.accountRemoved.summary: «Remove» took the pair off the actor.

event:ActorAccounts.accountStatusChanged.summary: «Block account» / «Unblock account» changed the pair's status.

event:ActorAccounts.accountTransferred.summary: «Transfer accounts» moved the pair, with its balance and history, to another actor.

event:ActorAccounts.createRequested.summary: The create CTA was pressed and the page intercepts creation (`createHandling: 'event'`). Never fires in the default embedded mode.

event:ActorAccounts.folderChanged.summary: A folder was opened, or the reader returned to the root (no `folderId`).

event:ActorAccounts.statisticalAccountRe.summary: One statistical account (Minimum, Maximum or Average) was removed from a pair — unticked in «Statistical accounts» (once per type).

event:ActorAccounts.statisticalAccountsC.summary: «Statistical accounts» created Minimum / Maximum / Average accounts on a pair.

event:ActorAccounts.transactionSelected.summary: A row was activated inside the «Show transactions» history dialog.

event:ActorAccounts.triggersChanged.summary: «Manage triggers» changed a trigger of a pair: attached, unlinked, created (and bound) or edited. `triggerId` is the trigger actor; `level` says where it is bound — `account`, the actor's own account, or `pair`, every actor's account of the pair.

event:ActorFilterEditor.closed.summary: The editor closed — after a save, or without one.

event:ActorFilterEditor.filterSaved.summary: A filter was created or updated.

event:ActorList.actorClick.summary: Fired when an actor row is single-clicked — the page's own click handling under `rowClickAction: 'event'`.

event:ActorList.actorCreated.summary: An actor was created from the list's «Create actor» (on a Scripts list: «Create smart form», whose `actorId` is the new form's `appId` and which also carries its `ref`; on a Graphs list: «Create graph», the new graph — bind it to the graph editor to land on its first layer).

event:ActorList.actorDoubleClick.summary: Fired when an actor row is double-clicked — the page's own handling under `rowDoubleClickAction: 'event'`.

event:ActorList.exportQueueOpened.summary: «Open» was pressed on «Added to the export queue» (with `exportQueueLink`): show the queue. Last, so a binding added in an editor still starts on the block's primary event.

event:ActorList.rowAction.summary: One of `rowActions` was chosen on a row — ActorView's `onAction` shape, plus the row's `ref` and `formId` (a page building a link to the actor needs them, and has no read of its own).

event:ActorView.backRequested.summary: Native Back was pressed; ask requestLeave before navigating away.

event:ActorView.formAdded.summary: Fires when a form is added on the event's Forms tab: `formActorId` was created from the event form `formId` and pinned to the event `actorId`. Also announced as `onChildEvent` `form-added`.

event:ActorView.formOpened.summary: Fires when the reader opens one of the event's forms — expands its row or opens the form actor. Also announced as `onChildEvent` `form-opened`.

event:ActorView.leaveResolved.summary: Fires in answer to `requestLeave`; `requestId` matches the request and `allowed` says whether the page may leave.
event:ActorView.leaveResolved.body: `allowed` is `true` when nothing was unsaved or the user chose to discard it.

event:ActorView.onAction.summary: Fires when the user chooses one of the `header.actions`; `actionId` names it.
event:ActorView.onAction.body: `actorId` and `accId` identify the actor, and `invocationId` is unique to each choice.

event:ActorView.onChildEvent.summary: Fires when something happens inside one of the actor's sections, such as a save, a removal or a sent comment.
event:ActorView.onChildEvent.body:
`section` says where (`actor`, `settings`, `smartForm`, `reactions`, `access`, or the id of
an `attachments` / `accounts` tab) and `type` what happened; the other fields carry that
event's details, e.g. `message` for `error` and the written fields for `actor-updated`.

event:ActorView.onTabChange.summary: Fires when the open tab changes, by the user or a fallback to Details; `tabId` is the new tab.
event:ActorView.onTabChange.body: Fires together with `sectionChanged`, which carries the same id as `section`.

event:Attachments.fileOpened.summary: A file was opened in the viewer.

event:Avatar.onClick.summary: Fires when the avatar is clicked, or activated with Enter/Space (wiring it makes the avatar a focusable button); `$event` is the DOM click event, from which an expression cannot read anything useful.

event:Banner.onClose.summary: Fires when the close button is clicked (a `flush` banner shows that button only when this is wired); `$event` is the DOM click event, from which an expression cannot read anything useful. The banner does not hide itself — the chain must.

event:Breadcrumbs.onChange.summary: Fires when a breadcrumb is clicked — never the current (last or `current`) or a `disabled` one; `$event` is `{ id, index }`, the item's `id` and its position in `items` (counted over the full list, even when collapsed by `maxItems`).

event:Button.onBlur.summary: Fires when the button loses focus; `$event` is the DOM focus event, from which an expression cannot read anything useful.

event:Button.onClick.summary: Fires when the button is clicked, but not while it is disabled or `loading`; `$event` is the DOM click event, from which an expression cannot read anything useful.

event:Button.onFocus.summary: Fires when the button receives focus; `$event` is the DOM focus event, from which an expression cannot read anything useful.

event:Button.onMouseEnter.summary: Fires when the pointer moves onto the button; `$event` is the DOM mouse event, from which an expression cannot read anything useful.

event:Button.onMouseLeave.summary: Fires when the pointer moves off the button; `$event` is the DOM mouse event, from which an expression cannot read anything useful.

event:CallTranscription.unreadChanged.summary: Lines that arrived while the surface was hidden — a badge for the host.

event:Card.onClick.summary: Fires when the card is clicked — or, when `interactive`, activated with Enter/Space; `$event` is the DOM event, from which an expression cannot read anything useful.

event:ChangeJournal.actorClick.summary: Fired when a referenced actor in the feed is activated. The block owns no routing, so where that goes is the page's to decide — bind this to `navigate.local`, `overlay.open` or a `widget.call` on the block that can show the actor.

event:ChangeJournal.filterChanged.summary: Fired whenever the applied filter changes, including via `setFilter`.

event:Chart.error.summary: Fires when the dashboard's configuration or data fails to load or is invalid.
event:Chart.error.body: `$event.message` describes the failure; the block shows its own error state.

event:Chart.metricClick.summary: A viewer clicked one dashboard metric — a bar, a point, a sector, a table row or a KPI card. Emitted whether or not `drillDown` opens anything, so a page can react to every click.

event:Chart.ready.summary: Fires when the dashboard's configuration has loaded, and again whenever it is re-read.
event:Chart.ready.body: `$event.actorId` is the dashboard; `$event.chartType` is its chart type.

event:Chart.transactionSelected.summary: A row of the drill-down list was chosen: a transaction `id` in `transactions` mode, or a `transferId` in `transfers` mode.

event:Checkbox.onChange.summary: Fires when the user checks or unchecks the box; `$event` is `{ value }`, the new checked state as a boolean.

event:Chip.onClick.summary: Fires when the chip is clicked (wiring it makes the chip clickable); `$event` is the DOM click event, from which an expression cannot read anything useful.

event:ColorPalette.selected.summary: A colour was chosen, from either section. `color` is absent when the choice was cleared.

event:ColorPicker.onCancel.summary: Fires when the Cancel button is clicked or the user clicks outside the picker (wiring this shows the Cancel button); `$event` is empty.

event:ColorPicker.onChange.summary: Fires on every colour change while the user drags or types in the picker; `$event` is `{ hex, rgb }` — `hex` a `#RRGGBBAA` string (`#RRGGBB` with `disableAlpha`) and `rgb` an `{ r, g, b, a }` object.

event:ColorPicker.onSave.summary: Fires when the OK button is clicked (wiring this shows that button); `$event` is the current colour as `{ hex, rgb }`.

event:CreateAccount.accountCreated.summary: The pair exists on the actor (and, with `offerAccess`, the reader is done with access).

event:CreateAccount.closed.summary: The dialog closed — after a create, a cancel, or the `close` api.

event:CreateActor.actorCreated.summary: Fired once per created actor — including every submit-and-continue action.

event:CreateActor.actorUpdated.summary: Fired once after an existing actor is updated.

event:CreateActor.closed.summary: The application requested its host to close (X/API, or a primary-action success).

event:CreateEvent.closed.summary: Requested its host to close (X/API, or a successful submit).

event:CreateEvent.eventCreated.summary: Fires when a new event has been saved; the form then closes.
event:CreateEvent.eventCreated.body: `$event.eventId` is the new event actor's id.

event:CreateEvent.eventUpdated.summary: Fires when changes to the edited event (`actorId`) have been saved; the form then closes.

event:CreateSmartForm.closed.summary: The dialog closed — after a create, a cancel, or the `close` api.

event:CreateSmartForm.smartFormCreated.summary: The smart form exists: `appId` is what `SmartFormEditor {appId}` opens.

event:CreateTransaction.closed.summary: The form asked its host to close — the modal's `Cancel`, the `close` api, or a successful write (a modal closes on success, as the modal it replaces did).

event:CreateTransaction.fieldTransferCre.summary: A form-field transfer was written: the values of `from` legs' fields moved into the `to` legs' fields. `id` is a string UUID.

event:CreateTransaction.modeChanged.summary: Fired whenever the mode changes, including via `switchMode`.

event:CreateTransaction.submitFailed.summary: A submit did not produce an entry. Paired with the two success events so a page can react to either outcome without polling state.
event:CreateTransaction.submitFailed.body:
- `invalid` — the draft did not validate, or an amount breached an account
 limit. Nothing was sent.
- `declined` — the write reached the ledger and the ledger REFUSED it. Not a
 transport problem: retrying the same draft will be refused again.
- `failed` — the write was attempted and could not be confirmed.

event:CreateTransaction.transactionCreat.summary: A ledger transaction was written. `id` is a number.

event:CreateTransaction.transferCreated.summary: A transfer was written. `id` is a string UUID — unlike a transaction's numeric id.
event:CreateTransaction.transferCreated.body:
`from`/`to` are LISTS because a transfer is N sources → M targets. Both sides always
share `currencyId`; that invariant is enforced before submit.

event:DashboardWizard.dashboardSaved.summary: A chart was created or updated through the wizard.

event:DatePicker.onCancel.summary: Fires when the Cancel button is clicked or Escape is pressed in the calendar, after the pending selection is discarded; `$event` is empty.

event:DatePicker.onChange.summary: Fires only when the user confirms with OK, never while picking and never with `null`; `$event` is `{ startDate, endDate, timeZoneOffset, recurrence? }` — Unix seconds (`endDate` equals `startDate` for a single date), the offset in minutes, and `recurrence` present only when the `recurrence` prop is on (`null` while Repeat is off).

event:DatePicker.onOk.summary: Fires when the OK button is clicked, after `onChange` (and even when nothing was picked); `$event` is empty.

event:DragDropZone.onClick.summary: Fires when a `clickable` zone is clicked or activated with Enter/Space (also opening the file dialog when `enableFileInput` is on); `$event` is the DOM event, from which an expression cannot read anything useful.

event:DragDropZone.onDragEnter.summary: Fires once when a drag first enters the zone (not again for its children); `$event` is the DOM drag event, from which an expression cannot read anything useful.

event:DragDropZone.onDragLeave.summary: Fires once when the drag finally leaves the zone; `$event` is the DOM drag event, from which an expression cannot read anything useful.

event:DragDropZone.onDragOver.summary: Fires continuously while a drag moves over the zone; `$event` is the DOM drag event, from which an expression cannot read anything useful.

event:DragDropZone.onDrop.summary: Fires when files are dropped on the zone, or picked through its file dialog when `enableFileInput` is on; `$event` is the browser `FileList` of those files (live `File` objects, not plain data), and `accept` is not applied to drops.

event:ESign.documentSigned.summary: The provider confirmed the user's signature.

event:ESign.signCancelled.summary: The user closed the widget, or the dialog while the document was prepared, before signing.

event:EventsCalendar.eventChanged.summary: The reader moved or resized an event in the calendar — a neighbouring block showing it should refresh.

event:EventsCalendar.eventCreated.summary: An event was created or edited from the calendar.

event:EventsCalendar.eventOpened.summary: The reader opened an event (from its peek card, or directly under `rowClickAction: 'event'`).

event:EventsCalendar.rangeChanged.summary: The shown period changed (navigation or a view switch). `date` is the day it is anchored on — bind the `date` prop to it for a route-backed period (`from` is the grid's first day, often in the previous month).

event:EventsList.chatOpened.summary: In the compact chat list: a conversation was opened from the contact picker — found, or created when there was none. The list has already opened it (unless `rowClickAction: 'event'`, where the page shows it) and re-read itself for a new one.

event:EventsList.eventCreated.summary: An event was created from the list's «Add event».

event:EventsList.eventOpened.summary: The list opened an event, and on what: its details (a row of the feed, a card's Details), its Meeting (Join) or its conversation (a row of the chat list). Not under `rowClickAction: 'event'`, where the list opens nothing — `eventSelected` / `meetingJoin` / `chatOpened` say what the reader picked.

event:EventsList.eventSelected.summary: Fires when the reader opens an event by activating its title in a row (click or keyboard) — in the chat list, by picking a chat or a contact. Contact picks also emit `chatOpened` with creation metadata.
event:EventsList.eventSelected.body:
`$event.eventId` is the event actor's id; bind it to whatever shows the event. Emitted in
every `rowClickAction` — it is the page's own click handling under `event`, where a call card's
Join (or a live-call chip) emits it too when the host does not open calls itself (before
`meetingJoin`), so a page that binds only this one still opens the event from it. The runtime
opens calls itself, on the event's Meeting tab, and then neither event is emitted.

event:EventsList.meetingJoin.summary: The reader chose to join an event's call — a call card's or a meeting row's Join. The list has already opened the event on its Meeting, entering the room (unless `rowClickAction: 'event'`, where the host does — the runtime, emitting nothing — or else the page, after `eventSelected`).

event:EventsList.starToggled.summary: A row's star was toggled and the server has stored it (a failed write rolls back, unannounced).

event:EventsList.streamChanged.summary: With `streams`: the reader picked another stream on the bar. `parent` is its tab — itself, or `sign` / `globalLive` for a sub-stream. Bind `stream` to it for a route-backed tab.

event:EventsList.viewChanged.summary: The reader switched between the list and the calendar (`viewSwitch`). Bind `view` to it for a route-backed choice.

event:GraphEditor.back.summary: The native return button was activated.

event:GraphEditor.layerOpened.summary: Fired when the open layer changes.

event:GuestJoin.joined.summary: The viewer may now open the actor — the page routes them there.

event:GuestJoin.waiting.summary: The viewer is in the waiting room.

event:HubNavigation.onSelect.summary: Ordinary activation; $event is the selected item id. Modified clicks use the item's href.

event:ImportExport.actorClick.summary: A finished task's graph or event was opened from its details panel. The block owns no routing, so where that goes is the page's to decide — bind this to `navigate.local`, `overlay.open` or a `widget.call` on the block that can show the actor.

event:ImportExport.importStarted.summary: An import was enqueued. Carries the task id and nothing else — never the archive's credentials.

event:ImportExport.taskFinished.summary: A task this client watched reach a terminal state.

event:MeetingRoom.actorUpdated.summary: New actor data from a nested moderator write.

event:MeetingRoom.left.summary: Explicit Leave, not a surface unmount or navigation.

event:Modal.onCancel.summary: Fires when the footer Cancel button is clicked (wiring this shows that button); `$event` is the DOM click event, from which an expression cannot read anything useful.

event:Modal.onClose.summary: Fires when the user dismisses the modal — header close button, Escape, or a click on the backdrop; `$event` carries nothing usable. The modal does not close itself — the chain must.

event:Modal.onOk.summary: Fires when the footer OK button is clicked (wiring this shows that button); `$event` is the DOM click event, from which an expression cannot read anything useful.

event:NavMenu.onClick.summary: Fires after every click on an enabled item, following `onSelect` and any expand/collapse; `$event` is the item's `id`.

event:NavMenu.onExpandToggle.summary: Fires together with `onOpenChange` when an item with children is expanded or collapsed; `$event` is the item's `id` — the new expanded state is not passed.

event:NavMenu.onOpenChange.summary: Fires when clicking an item with children expands or collapses it; `$event` is the item's `id` — the new open state is not passed.

event:NavMenu.onSelect.summary: Fires when an enabled item is clicked, including a parent item and the already-selected one; `$event` is the item's `id`.

event:NotificationCenter.allRead.summary: Every entry of a workspace (`accId`), or of every workspace shown, was marked read.

event:NotificationCenter.notificationOpe.summary: The reader opened an entry. Its actor's entries are already marked read; bind this to what shows the actor — `$event.actorId` (for a reaction, the actor it was left on; `reactionId` names the reaction itself), in workspace `$event.accId`.

event:Pagination.onChange.summary: Fires when the user moves to another page (not when re-choosing the current one); `$event` is the new 1-based page number.

event:Pagination.onPageSizeChange.summary: Fires when the user picks a page size in the size changer (`showSizeChanger`); `$event` is the new page size as a number.

event:Popover.onToggle.summary: Fires when the popover opens or closes (after the show/hide delay on a hover trigger); `$event` is `true` when opening and `false` when closing.

event:ProgressBar.onClose.summary: Fires when the close icon beside the status text is clicked (shown only with `statusText` and `closeIcon`); `$event` is the DOM click event, from which an expression cannot read anything useful.

event:Radio.onChange.summary: Fires when the user picks an enabled option; `$event` is that option's `value` as written in `options` (a bare value, not `{ value }`).

event:Reactions.modeChange.summary: Fired when opening or leaving a thread so a host-level mode switcher can stay in sync.

event:Reactions.reactionSent.summary: Fired after sim-api confirms a newly created reaction.

event:Reactions.threadChange.summary: Fired whenever the comments projection opens or closes a thread.

event:SearchEntity.resultSelected.summary: Fired when a result is picked.

event:Select.onBlur.summary: Fires when the field loses focus; `$event` is the DOM focus event, from which an expression cannot read anything useful.

event:Select.onChange.summary: Fires when the selection changes — an option picked or toggled, a tag removed, or the field cleared; `$event` is `{ value }`, the new value (an array when `multiple`; `undefined`, or `[]` when `multiple`, after a clear).

event:Select.onClear.summary: Fires when the clear button (`clearable`) drops the selection, after `onChange`; `$event` is empty. Clearing only the typed query in an open search does not fire it.

event:Select.onDeselect.summary: Fires in `multiple` mode when an option is removed, by unticking it or removing its tag; `$event` is that option's bare `value`.

event:Select.onDropdownVisibleChange.summary: Fires when the dropdown opens or closes; `$event` is `true` when it opens and `false` when it closes.

event:Select.onFocus.summary: Fires when the field receives focus; `$event` is the DOM focus event, from which an expression cannot read anything useful.

event:Select.onKeyDown.summary: Fires on each key press in the field; `$event` is the DOM keyboard event, from which an expression cannot read anything useful.

event:Select.onSearch.summary: Fires as the user types in the search field (`searchable`), and with `''` when the query is reset; `$event` is the current search string.

event:Select.onSelect.summary: Fires when the user picks an option (in `multiple` mode, only when adding one), right after `onChange`; `$event` is that option's bare `value`, not `{ value }`.

event:SelectAccount.changed.summary: Fired when the committed set changes, with its new size.

event:SelectAccount.picked.summary: Fired when a pair is picked / added.

event:SelectAccountTemplate.createAccoun.summary: Fired when the user asks to create a new template (host opens the editor).

event:SelectAccountTemplate.picked.summary: Fired when a template is picked.

event:SelectActor.createActorRequested.summary: Fired when the user asks for a creation surface the host must open.

event:SelectActor.picked.summary: Fired when an actor is picked — `created` marks a brand-new one.

event:SelectActorAccount.cleared.summary: Fired when the selection is dropped, by the field's cross or the `clear` api.

event:SelectActorAccount.picked.summary: Fired when a pair is picked (by the user or a resolved `select`).

event:SelectActorField.cleared.summary: Fired when the selection is dropped, by the field's cross, the `clear` api or a new actor.

event:SelectActorField.picked.summary: Fired when a field is picked (by the user or a resolved `select`).

event:SelectUser.selectionCleared.summary: Fired when the selection is cleared.

event:SelectUser.valueChanged.summary: Fired when a pick (or an imperative `setValue`) changes the selection.

event:Sharing.accessGranted.summary: Fired after a grant, or after an existing subject's privileges change, is saved.

event:Sharing.accessRevoked.summary: Fired after a revoke is saved.

event:Sharing.linkGenerated.summary: A public link was created or replaced — the old one, if any, no longer works.

event:Slider.onChange.summary: Fires continuously as the user drags a thumb or edits the number field (`showInput`); `$event` is the new value as a number, or a `[from, to]` pair when `range` is on.

event:SmartForm.dirtyChanged.summary: Fires when the form gains or loses unsaved input; `dirty` is the new value.
event:SmartForm.dirtyChanged.body: Also fires with `false` when the user closes or retries the form, and when the block is removed.

event:SmartForm.failed.summary: Fires when the running form reports an error; `message` is its text.
event:SmartForm.failed.body:
Does not fire when the form's details cannot be read — the block then only shows its error
banner with Retry.

event:SmartForm.submitted.summary: Fires when the user submits the form.

event:SmartFormEditor.back.summary: The native return button was activated.

event:SmartFormEditor.deleted.summary: The form was deleted from the editor's menu (to the trash); `corezoidProjectId` when its project went too.

event:SmartFormEditor.dirtyChanged.summary: Fires on open and whenever the form gains or loses unsaved edits; `dirty` is the new value.

event:SmartFormEditor.pageOpened.summary: Fires when the editor opens another page, through `openPage` or the user's navigation; `pageId` names it.

event:SmartFormEditor.published.summary: Fires after the user confirms a publish and the release is created; `releaseId` is the new release.

event:SmartFormEditor.saved.summary: Fires when files are written to the server, by autosave or `save`; `fileIds` lists them.

event:SmartFormEditor.selectionChanged.summary: Fires when the selected node changes; `nodeId` is the new selection, or `null` when none.

event:SmartFormEditor.themeChanged.summary: Fires when the user edits theme tokens, before they are saved; `tokenIds` lists the changed tokens.

event:SmartFormEditor.validityChanged.summary: Fires on open and whenever the validation result changes; carries `valid` and `issueCount`.

event:Splitter.onResize.summary: Fires continuously while a split bar is dragged; `$event` is the updated array of panel sizes, one per panel (a number or a CSS size such as `'40%'`).

event:Splitter.onResizeEnd.summary: Fires when the user releases a split bar; `$event` is the final array of panel sizes, one per panel (a number or a CSS size such as `'40%'`).

event:Splitter.onResizeStart.summary: Fires when the user starts dragging a split bar; `$event` is the array of panel sizes before the drag, one per panel (a number or a CSS size such as `'40%'`).

event:Streams.streamChanged.summary: The reader picked another stream. `parent` is its tab: itself, or `sign` / `globalLive` for a sub-stream.

event:TabItem.onClick.summary: Fires on every click of this tab, including when it is already active (unlike the parent `Tabs`' `onChange`); `$event` is the DOM click event, from which an expression cannot read anything useful.

event:Table.onScroll.summary: Fires as the table body scrolls; `$event` is the DOM scroll event, from which an expression cannot read anything useful.

event:Table.onSort.summary: Fires when the user clicks the header of a `sortable` column, cycling ascending → descending → unsorted; `$event` is the column's `dataIndex`, falling back to its `key` — the direction is not passed.

event:Tabs.onChange.summary: Fires when the user clicks a tab other than the current one (re-clicking the active tab does not fire); `$event` is the clicked tab's `value` as a bare string, not `{ value }`.

event:TextInput.onBlur.summary: Fires when the field loses focus; `$event` is the DOM focus event, from which an expression cannot read anything useful.

event:TextInput.onChange.summary: Fires on every edit of the field's text; `$event` is `{ value }`, the new text as a string — also for the numeric types, after the input is sanitised.

event:TextInput.onClear.summary: Fires when the clear button (`allowClear`, shown on hover or focus while the field has a value) is clicked; `$event` is the DOM click event, from which an expression cannot read anything useful. The field does not empty itself — the chain must reset `value`.

event:TextInput.onExpandClick.summary: Fires when the expand chevron shown by `expandIcon` is clicked; `$event` is the DOM click event, from which an expression cannot read anything useful.

event:TextInput.onFocus.summary: Fires when the field receives focus; `$event` is the DOM focus event, from which an expression cannot read anything useful.

event:TextInput.onInput.summary: Fires on every edit, like `onChange`, but `$event` is the raw DOM input event, from which an expression cannot read anything useful — use `onChange` for the value.

event:TextInput.onKeyDown.summary: Fires on each key press in the field; `$event` is the DOM keyboard event, from which an expression cannot read anything useful.

event:TextInput.onKeyUp.summary: Fires on each key release in the field; `$event` is the DOM keyboard event, from which an expression cannot read anything useful.

event:ThemePicker.onChange.summary: Fires after the viewer switches to a different theme and the host has applied it; `$event` is `{ value }`, the chosen theme's id.

event:Toast.onClose.summary: Fires when the toast's close button is clicked; `$event` is the toast's `id`, or `''` when it has none.

event:Toggle.onChange.summary: Fires when the user flips an enabled toggle; `$event` is the DOM change event, from which an expression cannot read anything useful — unlike `Checkbox`, the new state is not passed, so derive it from the current `value`.

event:TransactionView.accountHistoryOpen.summary: «Account history» from the menu — open a `TransactionsList` scoped to this account.

event:TransactionView.actorOpened.summary: An actor the view names was pressed (the hero's, or a leg's on the Transfer tab). The app already shows it in a modal; bind this only to hear about it, not to navigate.

event:TransactionView.correctiveCreated.summary: A corrective transaction was written against the shown one.

event:TransactionView.repeat.summary: Repeat was pressed; the prefilled create-transaction form is opening.

event:TransactionView.transactionOpened.summary: A parent or child transaction was opened from the Linked tab (the view already shows it).

event:TransactionView.transferOpened.summary: «Open transfer» on the Transfer tab — route to a transfer view.

event:TransactionsList.entryCreated.summary: An entry was written from the list's «Create …» — `mode` is the list's mode at the time.
