A pair holds a debit AND a credit account, and only the page knows which one the form is about to write. `'total'` — the pair as a whole, for a page that only reads it (no side is missing, the balance is the pair's total).

prop:SelectActorAccount.invalid.summary: Paint the field as failing validation. Pair it with `helperText` — see below.

prop:SelectActorAccount.label.summary: Form-field label above the field, rendered by `Select` as a real `<label for>`. A page that puts its own text beside the block instead gets no association — and in a form holding both actor pickers, the two labels would not even render alike.

prop:SelectActorAccount.labels.summary: Per-label text overrides; every entry optional, falling back to the active language.

prop:SelectActorAccount.required.summary: Draw the required marker in the label.

prop:SelectActorAccount.showBalance.summary: Show the selected account's balance under the field. Off by default: only a page whose leg is fixed up front can honestly show one — legacy's transaction modal picks the side AFTER the account, so it shows none.

prop:SelectActorField.accId.summary: Workspace id whose actor is read. Falls back to the active workspace.

prop:SelectActorField.actorId.summary: The actor whose fields are offered. Absent ⇒ the field is inert and says so.

prop:SelectActorField.helperText.summary: Supporting or validation text under the field — where an `invalid` page's message goes.

prop:SelectActorField.invalid.summary: Paint the field as failing validation. Pair it with `helperText`.

prop:SelectActorField.label.summary: Form-field label above the field, rendered by `Select` as a real `<label for>`.

prop:SelectActorField.labels.summary: Per-label text overrides; every entry optional, falling back to the active language.

prop:SelectActorField.required.summary: Draw the required marker in the label.

prop:SelectUser.accId.summary: Workspace id whose users (and groups) are listed. Falls back to the active workspace.

prop:SelectUser.allowGroups.summary: Also offer groups in a second independently scrolling column, stacked when narrow.

prop:SelectUser.disabled.summary: Render the field as disabled: it shows the selection but cannot be opened or changed.

prop:SelectUser.hiddenSubjects.summary: Subjects omitted from the available choices; useful for excluding the current user.

prop:SelectUser.labels.summary: Per-label text overrides; every entry is optional and falls back to the kit dictionary for the active language — `{ "labels": { "title": "{{ $locale.title }}" } }`.
prop:SelectUser.labels.body:
A `record`, not a hand-listed key set: the authoritative list is `SelectUserLabels` in the block
package, kept honest there by `SELECT_USER_LABEL_KEYS`'s `satisfies` check. Restating all of it
here is a fourth copy with nothing tying it to the interface — miss a key and its CDU
override is silently stripped at runtime, with no type error and no failing test. Unknown
keys are ignored by `resolveLabels`, which walks `SELECT_USER_LABEL_KEYS` rather than the payload.

prop:SelectUser.maxItems.summary: Caps how many subjects `multiple` may hold; a pick past the limit is ignored.

prop:SelectUser.multiple.summary: Allow more than one subject to be selected, shown as chips.

prop:SelectUser.placeholder.summary: Text the empty field shows while closed.
prop:SelectUser.placeholder.body:
Omitted, the field reads «Select a user» in the active language. With `allowGroups`, an open
panel shows its own search hint instead.

prop:SelectUser.value.summary: The controlled selection — a single subject, several (pick order preserved), or none.

prop:Sharing.accId.summary: Workspace id the object belongs to. Falls back to the active workspace.

prop:Sharing.labels.summary: Per-label text overrides; every entry is optional and falls back to the kit dictionary for the active language — `{ "labels": { "title": "{{ $locale.title }}" } }`.
prop:Sharing.labels.body:
A `record`, not a hand-listed key set: the authoritative list is `SharingLabels` in the block
package, kept honest there by `SHARING_LABEL_KEYS`'s `satisfies` check. Restating all of it
here is a fourth copy with nothing tying it to the interface — miss a key and its CDU
override is silently stripped at runtime, with no type error and no failing test. Unknown
keys are ignored by `resolveLabels`, which walks `SHARING_LABEL_KEYS` rather than the payload.

prop:Sharing.objectId.summary: Actor uuid, numeric form id, or account `<nameId>_<currencyId>` pair.

prop:Sharing.objectType.summary: What kind of object `objectId` names: an `actor`, an Account Template (`form`), or an `account` name + currency pair.

prop:Sharing.ownerId.summary: The object's resource-owner user id (e.g. an actor's `ownerId`), as a string.

prop:Sharing.placement.summary: Popover placement for the "add access" search field (kit `Placements`).

prop:Sharing.publicLink.summary: Actors only: the actor's public link as a folded row under the grid — create, copy, replace and revoke it, and whether guests wait to be let in (they are admitted from the call room).

prop:Sharing.publicLinkDueDate.summary: Expiry (unix seconds) a created public link asks for — a meeting binds its end plus a grace period. Absent ⇒ sim-api's default.

prop:Sharing.publicLinkLabels.summary: Per-label overrides for the public link row; unknown keys are ignored.

prop:Slider.inputWidth.summary: Width of the input field in pixels

prop:Slider.marks.summary: A slider tick mark — the real `label` is a ReactNode, narrowed here to a string.

prop:Slider.range.summary: Whether the slider is in range mode (two thumbs) Automatically detected if value is an array

prop:Slider.showTooltip.summary: Whether to show tooltip on hover

prop:Slider.value.summary: Current value of the slider Can be a single number or array of two numbers for range mode

prop:SmartForm.accId.summary: Workspace id. Falls back to the active workspace from the host.

prop:SmartForm.active.body:
`false` keeps an open form on screen but inert, and holds back `settings.autorun`.

Default: `true`.

prop:SmartForm.actorId.summary: The actor the form runs for — for a form on a comment, the comment (reaction) id.

prop:SmartForm.appId.summary: The smart form (Script actor) to run.
prop:SmartForm.appId.body:
The block shows the form's title with an Open button and runs the form once opened, in place,
through the host's smart-form runtime. A CDU v1 (legacy) form carries a "Legacy" chip and runs
only when the host shows legacy forms (the runtime does, through the legacy app); otherwise the
block says that format cannot be displayed here, and in a host with no smart-form runtime it
says that host cannot run smart forms.

prop:SmartForm.labels.summary: Per-key copy overrides for the block's own text, such as `title`, `open`, `close` and `failed`.
prop:SmartForm.labels.body:
The keys are `title`, `open`, `close`, `loading`, `failed`, `unavailable`, `noRuntime`, `legacyUnsupported`,
`legacyBadge` and `legacyHint` (the chip on a legacy form and its tooltip), `expired`,
`denied`, `retry`, and `discard`, `cancel` and `discardBody` for the dialog shown before
unsaved input is thrown away.

prop:SmartForm.rootActorId.summary: The actor the form belongs to: `actorId` itself, or for a form on a comment the actor holding that comment.

prop:SmartForm.settings.summary: When and for whom the form opens.
prop:SmartForm.settings.body:
`autorun` opens it as soon as the block scrolls into view; `expired` (Unix seconds) is a
deadline after which it can no longer be opened; `users` and `groups` restrict opening to
those user and group ids (the server's permissions still apply); `fullWidth: false` caps
the block's width.

prop:SmartFormEditor.accId.summary: Workspace id. Falls back to the active workspace from the host.

prop:SmartFormEditor.aiConsole.summary: Offer the AI console tab (S14). Enabled by default; a disabled flag loads none of its code.

prop:SmartFormEditor.appId.summary: The Script actor (smart form) being edited.

prop:SmartFormEditor.appKey.summary: The form's `appKey` — the `/sf/{appKey}` the Routes tab previews each route's short address under. It is minted by the backend at the first release, so a page binds it once it is known (absent ⇒ the tab shows a placeholder). Not a main Inspector field: it is bound from data, never typed by hand.

prop:SmartFormEditor.labels.summary: Per-key copy overrides keyed WITHOUT the `smartFormEditor.` prefix (`{ "state.dirty": "…" }`) — the seam a page localizes through, e.g. `{{ $locale.unsaved }}`.

prop:SmartFormEditor.mode.summary: How a page's tab opens: source, source + preview, or preview.

prop:SmartFormEditor.panel.summary: Tool window open on start: central Inspector/AI, theme tab, or History at the bottom.

prop:SmartFormEditor.previewVisible.summary: Whether a page's tab opens with the live preview: `true` opens source + preview, `false` the source alone.

prop:SmartFormEditor.runtimeOrigin.summary: Where the runtime serves smart forms, for Run and the form menu's "Open …" / "App link". Absent ⇒ the page's own origin: the editor is itself a page of that runtime.

prop:SmartFormEditor.showBack.summary: Show the editor’s native return button; emits `back` for the containing page.

prop:SmartFormEditor.surface.summary: Central workspace shown on open: the `inspector`, the `json` source, or the `ai` console.
prop:SmartFormEditor.surface.body:
Takes precedence over `view` and `panel`; `ai` falls back to `inspector` when `aiConsole` is
`false`. Unset, the editor reopens the layout the viewer last used, else the AI console (the
Inspector when `aiConsole` is `false`).

prop:SmartFormEditor.view.summary: Legacy authoring view on open: `json` opens on the JSON source; `outline` leaves the choice to the other props.
prop:SmartFormEditor.view.body:
Superseded by `surface` and `panel`, which win when set.

Default: `'outline'`.

prop:Space.bottom.summary: Whether to apply padding to the bottom side.
prop:Space.bottom.body: ⚠️ See left — setting one side turns the unspecified ones off. Prefer sides.

prop:Space.customSize.summary: Custom padding sizes for each side using CSS-like syntax - 1 value: all sides - 2 values: [vertical, horizontal] = [top/bottom, left/right] - 3 values: [top, horizontal, bottom] = [top, left/right, bottom] - 4 values: [top, right, bottom, left]
prop:Space.customSize.body: When customSize is provided, size and directional props (left/right/top/bottom) are ignored

prop:Space.fill.summary: Absolutely fill the nearest `positioned` ancestor (`position: absolute; inset: 0`) — a full-bleed layer such as a background behind content. Pair with `layer` to control stacking order.

prop:Space.fullHeight.summary: Whether the space should take full height

prop:Space.fullViewport.summary: Anchor the element to the full dynamic viewport height (`100dvh`, with a `100vh` fallback). Use on the outermost shell container.

prop:Space.fullWidth.summary: Whether the space should take full width

prop:Space.grow.summary: Grow to fill the free space of a flex parent (`flex: 1 1 0%`).

prop:Space.layer.summary: Stacking order for layered children: `back` (behind), `base` (content), `dock` (above). No default — z-index is applied only when set.

prop:Space.left.summary: Whether to apply padding to the left side.
prop:Space.left.body:
⚠️ Specifying any of `left`/`right`/`top`/`bottom` turns every
*unspecified* side off. `{ top: false }` therefore means "no padding at all", not "all sides but top". Prefer sides.

prop:Space.minHeight.summary: Allow shrinking below the content's intrinsic height by setting `min-height: 0`. Required for a nested scroll area inside a flex column.

prop:Space.minWidth.summary: Allow shrinking below the content's intrinsic width by setting `min-width: 0`. Required to let a flex child truncate its own children (e.g. an ellipsised Label inside a row).

prop:Space.positioned.summary: Establish a positioning context (`position: relative`) so a `fill` child can absolutely fill it. Use on the layered shell container.

prop:Space.right.summary: Whether to apply padding to the right side.
prop:Space.right.body: ⚠️ See left — setting one side turns the unspecified ones off. Prefer sides.

prop:Space.scroll.summary: Make the element scroll its overflow (`overflow: auto`) and shrink as a flex child (`min-width/height: 0`), so a scroll region "just works" without the usual min-size incantation.

prop:Space.scrollStyle.summary: Scrollbar appearance. Only meaningful together with `scroll`.

prop:Space.sticky.summary: Stick to the top of the nearest scroll container (`position: sticky; top: 0`). Use for section headers inside a `scroll` region. The element must carry its own background so scrolled content does not show through.

prop:Space.stickyBottom.summary: Stick to the bottom of the nearest scroll container (`position: sticky; bottom: 0`). Mirror of `sticky` for a bottom-anchored dock.

prop:Space.top.summary: Whether to apply padding to the top side.
prop:Space.top.body: ⚠️ See left — setting one side turns the unspecified ones off. Prefer sides.

prop:Stack.align.summary: Alignment of items along the cross axis

prop:Stack.fill.summary: Absolutely fill the nearest `positioned` ancestor (`position: absolute; inset: 0`) — a full-bleed layer such as a background behind content. Pair with `layer` to control stacking order.

prop:Stack.fullHeight.summary: Whether the stack should take full height

prop:Stack.fullViewport.summary: Anchor the element to the full dynamic viewport height (`100dvh`, with a `100vh` fallback). Use on the outermost shell container.

prop:Stack.fullWidth.summary: Whether the stack should take full width

prop:Stack.grow.summary: Grow to fill the free space of a flex parent (`flex: 1 1 0%`).

prop:Stack.justify.summary: Justification of items along the main axis

prop:Stack.layer.summary: Stacking order for layered children: `back` (behind), `base` (content), `dock` (above). No default — z-index is applied only when set.

prop:Stack.minHeight.summary: Allow shrinking below the content's intrinsic height by setting `min-height: 0`. Required for a nested scroll area inside a flex column.

prop:Stack.minWidth.summary: Allow shrinking below the content's intrinsic width by setting `min-width: 0`. Required to let a flex child truncate its own children (e.g. an ellipsised Label inside a row).

prop:Stack.positioned.summary: Establish a positioning context (`position: relative`) so a `fill` child can absolutely fill it. Use on the layered shell container.

prop:Stack.scroll.summary: Make the element scroll its overflow (`overflow: auto`) and shrink as a flex child (`min-width/height: 0`), so a scroll region "just works" without the usual min-size incantation.

prop:Stack.scrollStyle.summary: Scrollbar appearance. Only meaningful together with `scroll`.

prop:Stack.space.summary: Space (padding) configuration for the stack container Accepts all Space component props except children

prop:Stack.sticky.summary: Stick to the top of the nearest scroll container (`position: sticky; top: 0`). Use for section headers inside a `scroll` region. The element must carry its own background so scrolled content does not show through.

prop:Stack.stickyBottom.summary: Stick to the bottom of the nearest scroll container (`position: sticky; bottom: 0`). Mirror of `sticky` for a bottom-anchored dock.

prop:Stack.wrap.summary: Whether items should wrap to new lines

prop:Streams.allowCreate.summary: Offer creation of a new stream. Off for a read-only page.

prop:Streams.stream.summary: The stream it opens on; a changed prop switches it. Defaults to the type's All (`all` / `chats`).

prop:Streams.streamType.summary: Which list's streams: `events` (the Events screen) or `chats`. Defaults to `events`.

prop:TabItem.badge.summary: A badge beside the label — a count (`value`), a `dot`, or an icon by name — styled by `variant` and `type`.

prop:TabItem.endIcon.summary: Icon after the label, by its `@simulator-ui-kit/icons` export name; an unknown name shows no icon.

prop:TabItem.startIcon.summary: Icon before the label, by its `@simulator-ui-kit/icons` export name; an unknown name shows no icon.

prop:Table.columns.summary: Column descriptors with name-based header icons.

prop:Table.hoverable.summary: Whether to show row hover effect

prop:Table.rowKey.summary: Row key getter — narrowed to the string form (component allows `string | (r) => Key`).

prop:TextInput.allowClear.summary: Whether to show a clear button when the input has value Shows CloseIcon that clears the input value when clicked

prop:TextInput.endIcon.summary: Icon-registry name for the trailing icon → ComponentIconConfig (adapter resolves).

prop:TextInput.expandIcon.summary: Expand icon direction to display instead of endIcon Shows ArrowUp2Icon when 'up' or ArrowDown2Icon when 'down' Takes priority over endIcon when provided

prop:TextInput.helperTooltip.summary: Tooltip text to display next to helper text

prop:TextInput.hideSpinners.summary: Hides the visual stepper while preserving keyboard stepping.

prop:TextInput.loading.summary: Whether the input is in a loading state Shows spinner instead of icons when true

prop:TextInput.max.summary: Native maximum, primarily for date inputs.

prop:TextInput.maxDecimals.summary: Maximum number of fractional digits accepted by a float.

prop:TextInput.min.summary: Native minimum, primarily for date inputs.

prop:TextInput.startIcon.summary: Icon-registry name for the leading icon → ComponentIconConfig (adapter resolves).

prop:TextInput.step.summary: Increment used by the buttons and Up/Down keys.

prop:TextInput.type.summary: What the field takes: text kinds (`text`, `email`, `password`, `tel`, `url`, `search`, `date`) or a number (`integer`, `float`), which adds the number controls (`step`, `maxDecimals`, `hideSpinners`).
prop:TextInput.type.body: `onChange` still passes the value as a string.

prop:ThemePicker.label.summary: Visible label of the `select` variant, and the accessible name of every variant. Absent ⇒ the select shows none and the accessible name is the kit's "Theme".

prop:ThemePicker.variant.summary: How the themes are offered: `toggle`, `segmented` or `select`; `auto` picks by count (nothing for one theme, `toggle` for two, `segmented` for three or four, `select` for more).

prop:Toast.description.summary: Narrowed from ReactNode to plain text.

prop:Toast.helperText.summary: Narrowed from ReactNode to plain text.

prop:Toast.type.summary: Type variant controlling filled vs outlined styling.

prop:Toast.variant.summary: Visual style applied to the toast.

prop:Toggle.error.summary: Whether the toggle has an error state

prop:Toggle.labelPosition.summary: Position of the label relative to the toggle

prop:Toggle.value.summary: Whether the toggle is checked (controlled by value prop)

prop:Tooltip.hideDelay.summary: Delay in milliseconds before hiding the tooltip

prop:Tooltip.position.summary: Position of the tooltip relative to trigger element

prop:Tooltip.showDelay.summary: Delay in milliseconds before showing the tooltip

prop:Tooltip.value.summary: Content to display in the tooltip

prop:TransactionView.accId.summary: Workspace id. Falls back to the active workspace from the host.

prop:TransactionView.createdAt.summary: `createdAt` (ms) of that transaction — `transaction/get`'s partition hint. Bind a list row's `$event.createdAt`; a deep link without it can reach only the last ~12 months.

prop:TransactionView.showBack.summary: Show a back button in the header; pressing it fires `back`. For a page that shows the view in place of the list it was opened from.

prop:TransactionView.transactionId.summary: The transaction to show (a `transactionResponse.id`, as a string or number). Absent ⇒ an empty state.

prop:TransactionsList.accountId.summary: Workspace id. Falls back to the active workspace from the host. Named `accountId` (not `accId`) to match this block's own props — in this platform's domain language "account" IS the workspace (legacy routes are `/actors_graph/:acc/...`), distinct from a LEDGER account (a `nameId`/`currencyId` pair, never a single flat id).

prop:TransactionsList.accountPair.summary: One-pair form of `accountPairs`, ignored when that is non-empty.

prop:TransactionsList.accountPairs.summary: Scopes EVERY read to these accounts (name + currency) — a row matches any of them. They render as locked chips under the toolbar, and the Filters panel drops its own Accounts field. Omitted or empty ⇒ every account pair in the workspace, narrowed in Filters by the reader. Bind a `SelectAccount` block's `state.pairs` straight through (its `multiselect` mode for several): its published pair is a superset of this shape.

prop:TransactionsList.accountType.summary: Which side of the accounts to open on — `fact` (actual entries) or `plan`. The reader changes it in the Filters panel (Account type) unless `showAccountTypeSwitch` is off; their pick is kept in the block's route, so a reload or a copied link reopens it. A pick away from this side is a filter (a chip, one in the Filters count) that Clear all returns from.

prop:TransactionsList.actorId.summary: Scopes the initial view to one actor's OWN legs — seeds `filter.actorIds` with this single id, same as picking it in the Actor filter. With `accountPair` both must hold on the same leg, in transfers mode too.

prop:TransactionsList.allowCreate.summary: Offer the toolbar's «Create transaction» / «Create transfer» (opens the CreateTransaction block). Off for a read-only page.

prop:TransactionsList.field.summary: The field the list opens on, by its item id in the `formId` template (`select_1`, `ownerId`).

prop:TransactionsList.fieldFormId.summary: The template that OWNS `field` when it is inherited from a parent of `formId` — the parent's id, which its actors keep the value under. Omitted ⇒ the field is `formId`'s own.

prop:TransactionsList.formFieldsTab.summary: Offer the Form fields tab — the history of form-field values, a change of a field being its «transaction» — and the field filter on Transfers. Not offered under an account scope.

prop:TransactionsList.formId.summary: The account template of the field the list opens on (with `field`) — Form fields and the Transfers field filter.

prop:TransactionsList.labels.summary: Per-message text overrides — see this repo's i18n rule: a page localizes one string by binding it, e.g. `{ "labels": { "transactionsList.col.amount": "{{ $locale.amountLabel }}" } }`.

prop:TransactionsList.mode.summary: Which stream to open on. `formFields` needs `formFieldsTab`, and is not offered under an account scope (`accountPairs`, `accountPair`): a field's history has no account to keep to.

prop:TransactionsList.rowClickAction.summary: What a row click (or `selectRow`) does. `panel` (the default) opens the transaction or transfer beside the list in its view; `drill` replaces the list with it until its Back; `event` opens nothing, so the page handles `transactionSelected` itself (a page that lays out its own TransactionView). The opened entry is kept in the block's route, so the address can be copied.

prop:TransactionsList.showAccountTypeSwi.summary: Render the Filters panel's Account type field (Fact / Plan). Off pins the list to `accountType`: no chip, and neither Clear all nor a saved route moves it.

prop:TransferView.accId.summary: Workspace id. Falls back to the active workspace from the host.

prop:TransferView.showBack.summary: Show a back button in the header; pressing it fires `back`. For a page that shows the view in place of the list (or the transaction) it was opened from.

prop:TransferView.transferId.summary: The transfer to show (a `transferResponse.id`, a UUID). Wins over `transferRef`. Absent (and no `transferRef`) ⇒ an empty state.

prop:TransferView.transferRef.summary: …or the transfer's workspace-unique reference, read through `transfer/by-ref/get`.

prop:Triggers.accId.summary: Workspace id. Falls back to the active workspace from the host.

prop:Triggers.actorId.summary: The actor whose account or data field the triggers watch.

prop:Triggers.dataField.summary: One of the actor's data fields (a key of its `data`).

prop:Triggers.labels.summary: Per-message text overrides keyed by this block's message ids (`triggers.*`) — the seam a page localizes through, e.g. `{ "triggers.create": "{{ $locale.newAlert }}" }`.

prop:Triggers.listMaxHeight.summary: Height (px) past which the triggers list scrolls inside the block, so «Attach existing» and «Create trigger» stay in view on a target with many triggers. `null` lets the list grow with its content.

prop:Triggers.nameId.summary: The actor's account, by its pair: `nameId` with `currencyId`, or neither.

prop:Triggers.readOnly.summary: Hide every write — attach, create, edit, unlink, resend.

prop:Triggers.subject.summary: The line naming what the triggers belong to. Absent, the block writes its own («Triggers of Acme Ltd - Balance, USD»); a string replaces it; `null` or `''` hides it — for a page that already names the target in its own heading.

prop:Triggers.targetKind.summary: Pin the trigger type — for a page that offers its own type picker beside its account or field picker. Absent, the block starts on the account when one is given (else the field) and, given both, the reader switches between the two. For an account the reader also switches between its two levels — the actor's own account and the account pair every actor holding it shares, whose writes the block confirms first.

prop:Upload.accept.summary: Accepted file types (MIME types or extensions)

prop:Upload.acceptErrorText.summary: Error message for files with invalid type Can include {accept} placeholder for accepted types

prop:Upload.avatar.summary: Display uploaded images as circular avatars (for profile pictures)

prop:Upload.description.summary: Description text shown in the upload zone Supports placeholders: {acceptTypes}, {maxSize} Defaults to the `upload.description` message of the active language (English: '{acceptTypes} · Up to {maxSize}').

prop:Upload.dragDropLabel.summary: Main drag and drop label text

prop:Upload.fileList.summary: The files the field shows, empty by default. The field does not keep its own list: bind it to the view model and write `onChange`'s new list back, or picked files disappear.

prop:Upload.maxFileSizeErrorText.summary: Error message for files exceeding maxSize Can include {maxSize} placeholder for file size

prop:Upload.separatorText.summary: Word joined between the accent action and dragDropLabel ("Click to upload" + "or" + "drag and drop")

prop:Upload.uploadCompleteText.summary: Text shown when upload is complete

prop:Upload.uploadingText.summary: Accessible status label announced during file upload (the visible row shows the percent value)

prop:Webhooks.accId.summary: Workspace id the webhooks belong to. Falls back to the active workspace.

prop:Wordmark.name.summary: Brand name supplied by the host, including its localized spelling.

prop:WorkspaceSidebar.ai.summary: The AI assistant: a button beside the navigation that opens the AI Console in a panel at the end of the page, the same dialog on every page of the Smart Form (its actor is the dialog's parent) and kept open across them. Signed-in members only, on a page the runtime rendered. `{}` turns it on.

prop:WorkspaceSidebar.dock.summary: How the dock (`presentation: "dock"`) comes and goes. `behavior`: `overlay` (default) floats over the page and reveals from the bottom edge band; `inset` opens from its handle (0.3 s rest or a click), hides as soon as the pointer leaves it or the window, and while shown lifts floating screen controls (graph counts, call bar, …) above it. `placement`: the edge the dock sits on (a floating left rail reveals from the left edge band). `configurable`: the member picks both in the account menu, remembered per member.

prop:WorkspaceSidebar.exportQueueItem.summary: The id of the item that opens Import & Export: it carries a dot while the viewer's export queue holds anything (added with «Add to export queue», not exported yet).

prop:WorkspaceSidebar.notifications.summary: The notification bell beside the navigation (the dock's handle carries a dot while there is news) and «Notification settings» in the account menu. An opened entry shows its actor in the host's actor view. Signed-in members only. `{}` turns it on with the defaults.

prop:WorkspaceSwitcher.labels.summary: Per-label text overrides. Every entry is optional and falls back to the kit dictionary for the active language, so a page localizes a single string by binding it — `{ "labels": { "triggerCaption": "{{ $locale.workspaceCaption }}" } }` — without restating the rest. Mirrors `WorkspaceSwitcherLabels`.

prop:WorkspaceSwitcher.placement.summary: Where the panel opens relative to the trigger (kit `Placements`).

response:assign.title: Set a view-model value
response:assign.summary: Sets one value in the view model.
response:assign.body: Same paths as `state`; missing parents are created; `""`, `"/"` or `"vm"` replaces the whole view model.

response:assign.path.summary: Where to write: `status`, `vm.status` and `/status` are the same.

response:assign.value.summary: The value to write, as sent.

response:navigate.title: Go to a page
response:navigate.summary: Opens a page, an in-app path or an external URL — the same routing as `navigate.local`.

response:navigate.history.summary: `push` adds a history entry (default); `replace` replaces the current one.

response:navigate.query.summary: The URL query; every value must be a string.

response:navigate.to.summary: A page id of this Smart Form, an in-app path starting with `/`, or an external URL.

response:notify.title: Show a toast
response:notify.summary: Shows a toast, like the client `notify` — but every value, title and helper text included, is shown as sent.

response:patch.title: Patch the tree or view model
response:patch.summary: Applies a JSON Patch to the rendered tree or to the view model — atomically.
response:patch.body: If any op fails, none is applied (telemetry `renderer.patch.rollback`) and the next action still runs.

response:patch.ops.summary: The JSON Patch operations, at least one. Paths are JSON Pointers (`/rows/0/name`). For `tree` they start at the root node (`/props/title`, `/children/0/props/text`), for `vm` at the view model.

response:redirect.title: Leave the app
response:redirect.summary: Leaves the app for an absolute `http(s)` URL.

response:redirect.history.summary: Accepted; the runtime always opens the URL as a new navigation (`location.assign`).

response:redirect.url.summary: The URL; it must start with `http://` or `https://`.

response:vm.merge.title: Merge into the view model
response:vm.merge.summary: Deep-merges an object into the view model.
response:vm.merge.body: Nested objects merge key by key; arrays, scalars and `null` replace; no key is ever removed.

response:vm.merge.patch.summary: The object to merge into the view model.

state:AccountDetails.accountType.summary: The side currently showing — `plan` for a plan-only pair, even when `fact` was asked for.

state:AccountDetails.isOpen.summary: Whether the panel is mounted. `modal` starts closed; `embedded` starts open.

state:AccountDetails.pair.summary: The pair the panel has read, for the side `accountType` names. Absent until `status` is `ready`.

state:AccountDetails.status.summary: What the panel is doing — `ready` once `pair` has been read. Absent while the panel is closed.

state:AccountTemplate.accessScope.summary: Whose access the Access tab shows: `template` or `actors` (the template's actors).

state:AccountTemplate.canModify.summary: Whether the user may change this template.
state:AccountTemplate.canModify.body:
Always `true` for a new template; for an existing one, the user's right to modify it, and
`false` for a system template.

state:AccountTemplate.dirty.summary: Whether the template, its access or its accounts have unsaved changes.

state:AccountTemplate.formId.summary: The id of the edited template; undefined for a new template until its first save.

state:AccountTemplate.issueCount.summary: The number of issues found in the template, warnings included.

state:AccountTemplate.title.summary: The template's title as currently edited, including unsaved changes.

state:AccountTemplate.valid.summary: Whether the template has no blocking issues and can be saved.

state:AccountTemplate.writeReady.summary: Whether the template can be saved right now.
state:AccountTemplate.writeReady.body:
Requires `canModify` and a server that accepts edits of this template. While `false` the
block is read-only and shows a warning.

state:AccountTemplatesList.filter.summary: The applied filter: `ownerIds`, and `createdFrom` / `createdTo` in unix seconds.
state:AccountTemplatesList.filter.body: `{}` when nothing is filtered; an omitted key is not filtered on.

state:AccountTemplatesList.query.summary: The current search text; `''` when not searching.

state:ActorAccounts.folderId.summary: The open folder; absent at the root.

state:ActorAccounts.query.summary: Current search text; `''` when not searching.

state:ActorFilterEditor.isOpen.summary: The editor is mounted. Embedded presentation starts open.

state:ActorFilterEditor.mode.summary: Whether the open editor creates a filter or edits one.

state:ActorList.openedActorId.summary: The actor currently open in the panel or detail; absent after closing or returning to the list.

state:ActorList.openedActorMode.summary: The current row's presentation; lets a host retain list chrome beside a panel and hide it only for drill-in.

state:Attachments.query.summary: Committed search query; `''` when not searching.

state:Attachments.selectedIds.summary: Ids of the currently selected rows.

state:Attachments.tab.summary: Active sub-tab of the actor scope.

state:ChangeJournal.field.summary: Applied field filter, or `null` for every field.

state:ChangeJournal.from.summary: Window start in ms of the applied filter.

state:ChangeJournal.to.summary: Window end in ms of the applied filter.

state:Chart.chartType.summary: The dashboard's chart type (`bar`, `line`, `pie`, `table`, `kpiCard`, …); undefined until it loads.

state:Chart.ready.summary: Whether the dashboard's configuration has loaded; `false` while loading and after an error.

state:Chart.title.summary: The dashboard's title; undefined until its configuration loads, and after an error.

state:ColorPalette.value.summary: The chosen colour, republished so other blocks can follow it.

state:CreateAccount.isOpen.summary: Whether the dialog is mounted. Embedded presentation starts open.

state:CreateActor.draft.summary: The current draft — everything the user has entered so far.

state:CreateActor.isOpen.summary: Whether the actor form application is mounted. Embedded presentation starts open.

state:CreateActor.mode.summary: Whether this instance creates a new actor or edits `props.actorId`.

state:CreateEvent.draft.summary: The event as currently typed: title, description, dates, fields, invites, attachments and links.
state:CreateEvent.draft.body:
Updates as the reader edits. In edit mode it starts from the loaded event; after a
successful save, a cancel or `close` it returns to its opening value.

state:CreateEvent.isSubmitting.summary: Whether a save is in flight.

state:CreateEvent.mode.summary: Whether this instance creates a new event or edits `props.actorId`.

state:CreateSmartForm.isOpen.summary: Whether the dialog is mounted. Embedded presentation starts open.

state:CreateTransaction.isOpen.summary: Whether the form is mounted. `modal` starts closed; `embedded` starts open.

state:CreateTransaction.submitting.summary: Whether a write is in flight.

state:CreateTransaction.valid.summary: Whether the draft would pass validation — what a host gates its own submit on.

state:ESign.busy.summary: An attempt is open: the document is prepared or the widget is signing.

state:ESign.canSign.summary: The user may start a signature now — what a page's own sign button is enabled by.

state:ESign.signedByMe.summary: The server has the user's signature on the actor.

state:ESign.status.summary: `signing` also while another block on the page signs this actor; `cancelled` is momentary — reported with `signCancelled`, then back to `idle`.

state:ESign.waiting.summary: Why the sign order keeps the user waiting, when it does.

state:EventsCalendar.openedEventId.summary: The event open in the calendar's detail, if any.

state:EventsList.selectedEventId.summary: The row painted as selected, by a click or by `select`.

state:EventsList.stream.summary: The stream the list shows: with `streams`, the bar's pick; without, the `stream` prop.

state:GraphEditor.focusActorId.summary: Actor currently requested as the deep-link focus.

state:GraphEditor.layerId.summary: The layer currently shown — readable as `$block.<id>.state.layerId`.

state:ImportExport.view.summary: Which side the block is showing: `import`, `export`, or nothing chosen yet (`none`).

state:MeetingRoom.view.summary: The actual pre-join or connected-room surface; changing a URL does not join or leave.

state:NotificationCenter.unreadCount.summary: Unread entries the block counts: the workspace's, or every workspace's under `all`.

state:SelectAccount.pairs.summary: The committed pairs. A single-mode selection publishes a one-element array (or empty).

state:SelectAccountTemplate.all.summary: The «All Account Templates» scope is selected.

state:SelectAccountTemplate.parents.summary: The picked Account Template's ancestor chain (immediate parent → … → root), populated only when `withParents` is set. A denied ancestor is an identity stub (no title).

state:SelectAccountTemplate.selectedId.summary: The selected Account Template id (undefined = nothing or «all» picked).

state:SelectActor.scopeFormId.summary: The template scope in force (undefined = the whole workspace).

state:SelectActor.selectedId.summary: The selected actor id (undefined = nothing selected).

state:SelectActor.selectedTitle.summary: The selected actor's title, for a page that renders the choice elsewhere.

state:SelectActorAccount.pair.summary: The committed pair, absent while nothing is selected.

state:SelectActorField.field.summary: The committed field, absent while nothing is selected.

state:SmartFormEditor.appId.summary: The Script actor (smart form) being edited.

state:SmartFormEditor.canModify.summary: Whether the user can edit the form.
state:SmartFormEditor.canModify.body: `false` on `production`, with `readonly`, or without the server-side right to modify the form.

state:SmartFormEditor.canRedo.summary: Whether the open file has an undone edit to redo.

state:SmartFormEditor.canUndo.summary: Whether the open file has an edit to undo.

state:SmartFormEditor.dirty.summary: Whether any file has unsaved edits.

state:SmartFormEditor.envTitle.summary: The environment being edited, `develop` or `production`, including after the user switches it.

state:SmartFormEditor.fileId.summary: The id of the open file, or `null` when nothing is open or the file is not saved yet.

state:SmartFormEditor.issueCount.summary: The number of validation issues across all files; a file that does not parse counts as one.

state:SmartFormEditor.mode.summary: How a page's tab shows: `code`, `split` or `preview`.

state:SmartFormEditor.pageId.summary: The page whose file is open, or `null` when the open file belongs to no page or nothing is open.

state:SmartFormEditor.panel.summary: The tool window in front: `theme` on the theme tab, `history` while History is open, else `inspector` or `ai`.

state:SmartFormEditor.previewVisible.summary: Whether the live preview is on screen; `false` in `split` mode when the editor is too narrow for it.

state:SmartFormEditor.selectedNodeId.summary: The id of the selected page node, or `null` when none is selected.

state:SmartFormEditor.valid.summary: Whether the form has no validation issues, i.e. `issueCount` is `0`.

state:SmartFormEditor.view.summary: `json` while the JSON source is the central workspace, otherwise `outline`.

state:Streams.stream.summary: The picked stream — bind an `EventsList`'s `stream` to it.

state:TransactionView.transactionId.summary: The transaction on screen — changes when a linked one is opened, or through `open`.

state:TransactionsList.filter.summary: The applied filter, including the reader's own changes and any `setFilter` call.
state:TransactionsList.filter.body:
Always has `accountType` (the `accountType` prop, `fact` by default, until the reader
switches it — Clear all returns to the prop's side) and opens on the current month (`from` /
`to`, unix ms); with `actorId` set, `actorIds` starts as that one actor.

state:TransferView.transferId.summary: The transfer on screen — changes through `open`.

state:Triggers.openTriggerId.summary: The trigger whose call history is open; absent on the list.

type:AccountDetails.title: Account Details
type:AccountDetails.summary: The read-only details of one account name + currency pair of an actor: status, Fact / Plan sides, limits, formula and balance.

type:AccountTemplate.title: Account Template Editor
type:AccountTemplate.summary: The Account Template constructor with a live preview.

type:AccountTemplatesList.title: Account Templates List
type:AccountTemplatesList.summary: The workspace’s Account Templates, with tabs, search and filters.

# E12-conditional-validation — Conditional / cross-field validation

**Goal.** Make one field required only in a specific branch: the free-text
"details" input is mandatory when the reason is `other`, and irrelevant
otherwise — with no conditional rules, by choosing which declared fields to check.

## Mechanisms

- **Unconditional rules** — both `type` and `details` are declared `required: true`
  on the `Form` (`id: "reason"`, `valueKey: "form"`).
- **`scope` decides what is checked** — Submit runs an `if`: for `other` it calls
  `form.validate` with `scope: ["type", "details"]`, otherwise `scope: ["type"]`.
  Rules apply to declared fields whether or not their input is mounted, so the
  `if` on the details input alone would not switch its rule off.
- **Branch-gated input** — the `details` `TextInput` carries
  `if: "vm.form.type = 'other'"`, so it is only on screen when it applies.
- **Clear stale values** — the reason `Select`'s `onChange` clears
  `vm.form.details` whenever the choice is not `other`.
- **`if` client action** gates the submit on `vm.valid.form` after validating.

## Page

The canonical page is [`pages/E12-conditional-validation.page.json`](pages/E12-conditional-validation.page.json); its line-by-line commented twin is
[`annotated/E12-conditional-validation.annotated.jsonc`](annotated/E12-conditional-validation.annotated.jsonc), which Storybook shows under _CDU v2 → Forms & validation_. CI keeps the two identical
once the comments are stripped, so the JSON is not repeated here.

## Expression breakdown

| Expression                                           | Evaluates to                            | Reactive on       |
| ---------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------- | ----------------- |
| `vm.form.type = 'other'` (details `if`, Submit `if`) | `true` only when reason is "other"      | `vm.form.type`    |
| `{{ vm.form.type }}` (Select value)                  | current reason value                    | `vm.form.type`    |
| `{{ vm.form.details }}` (input value)                | current details text                    | `vm.form.details` |
| `{{ vm.errors.form.details }}`                       | error string after validate, else empty | `vm.errors.form`  |
| `vm.valid.form = true` (`if` cond)                   | validity of the fields in `scope`       | `vm.valid.form`   |

## What your Corezoid process returns

`form.submit … "via": "corezoid"` runs the environment's Corezoid process with `path: "/send"`,
`body.formId` = the form id and `body.data` = a copy of the values. The process replies with a code
and, under `data.actions`, the response actions to apply (a top-level `actions` is ignored):

```json
{
  "code": 200,
  "data": {
    "actions": [
      { "type": "notify", "level": "success", "title": "Account closed" },
      { "type": "navigate", "to": "goodbye" }
    ]
  }
}
```

`onError` (the "Could not submit" toast) runs only when the call itself fails.

## Pitfalls

- Validating without `scope` checks `details` in the `standard` branch too — the
  form can then never be submitted there, with an error about a field the user
  cannot see.
- Unmounting `details` does not clear its value; without the clearing step in the
  `Select`'s `onChange`, text typed under `other` is still sent.
- `vm.valid.form` is written by `form.validate` (`setErrors` defaults to `true`) —
  read it _after_ that action in the chain, never before.

# E11-wizard — Multi-step wizard form

**Goal.** Walk a user through a form in three steps using a single view-model
counter (`vm.step`) and one shared `Form` — only the active step is on screen and
checked on Next, Back/Next never lose entered data, and Submit checks everything.

## Mechanisms

- **`if` per step section** — each step is a `Stack` gated by `if: "vm.step = N"`.
  A falsy `if` unmounts the node _and its subtree_, so the other steps' inputs do
  not exist while you are on the current one. Their **values** survive, because
  they live in the view model, not in the inputs.
- **One shared `Form`** (`valueKey: "wizard"`) wraps all three step sections.
  Every field's value lives at `vm.wizard.<name>`; child inputs are two-way bound
  (value binding + a `state` action on change).
- **Rules belong to declared fields, not to inputs** — `form.validate` without
  `scope` checks every declared field, mounted or not. So Next scopes the check to
  the step on screen: `scope: ["firstName", "lastName"]` on step 1,
  `["email", "company"]` on step 2, and advances only when `vm.valid.wizard = true`.
- **Submit checks the whole form** (no `scope`). Valid → `form.submit` via
  `corezoid`; invalid → jump to the first step with an error and warn.
- **`form.submit` does not validate itself**, and a non-2xx reply still runs
  `onSuccess` — so the success toast checks `$event.code`.

## Page

The canonical page is [`pages/E11-wizard.page.json`](pages/E11-wizard.page.json); its line-by-line commented twin is
[`annotated/E11-wizard.annotated.jsonc`](annotated/E11-wizard.annotated.jsonc), which Storybook shows under _CDU v2 → Forms & validation_. CI keeps the two identical
once the comments are stripped, so the JSON is not repeated here.

## Expression breakdown

| Expression                                 | Evaluates to                                  | Reactive on           |
| ------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------- | --------------------- |
| `Step {{ vm.step }} of 3`                  | `"Step 2 of 3"`                               | `vm.step`             |
| `vm.step = 1` (step-1 `if`)                | `true` only on step 1                         | `vm.step`             |
| `vm.step > 1` (Back `if`)                  | `false` on step 1, else `true`                | `vm.step`             |
| `vm.step < 3` (Next `if`)                  | `true` on steps 1–2                           | `vm.step`             |
| `{{ vm.step + 1 }}` / `{{ vm.step - 1 }}`  | next / previous step number                   | `vm.step`             |
| `{{ vm.wizard.firstName }}`                | current field value                           | `vm.wizard.firstName` |
| `{{ vm.errors.wizard.firstName }}`         | error string after validate, else empty       | `vm.errors.wizard`    |
| `vm.valid.wizard = true`                   | the verdict of the last `form.validate`       | `vm.valid.wizard`     |
| `$event.code >= 200 and $event.code < 300` | the process reported success (in `onSuccess`) | the reply             |

## What your Corezoid process returns

`form.submit … "via": "corezoid"` runs the environment's Corezoid process with `path: "/send"`,
`body.formId` = the form id and `body.data` = a copy of the values. The process replies with a code
and, under `data.actions`, the response actions to apply (a top-level `actions` is ignored):

```json
{
  "code": 200,
  "data": {
    "actions": [
      { "type": "vm.merge", "patch": { "step": 1, "wizard": {} } },
      { "type": "navigate", "to": "registration-done" }
    ]
  }
}
```

The actions are applied first, then the page's `onSuccess` runs with the reply as `$event`.
`onError` runs only when the call itself fails.

## Pitfalls

- `form.validate` without `scope` checks **every** declared field, including the
  steps not on screen — on Next that blocks step 1 with errors about step 3.
- `form.submit` does not validate; without the full `form.validate` before it, a
  field cleared on an earlier step is sent as is.
- `vm.step` is a **number** — compare with `=`/`<`/`>`, and advance with
  arithmetic (`{{ vm.step + 1 }}`), not string concatenation.

# E22-data-grid — Server-driven data grid (filter + sort + paginate)

**Goal.** Render a read-only tabular grid whose filtering, sorting and pagination are all
performed by the backend. The client keeps only the current page of rows plus a small `query`
descriptor; every toolbar interaction round-trips to `customer/list` and replaces `vm.rows` and `vm.total`.

## Mechanisms

- **`Table` primitive** for the tabular data — read-only, declarative `columns` + `dataSource`.
  Because there are no clickable rows, per-row buttons or badges-in-cells here, `Table` is the
  right tool (see the Pitfalls for when it is not).
- **`state` (merge)** to patch a single field of `vm.query` without rebuilding the whole object.
- **`simapi.call` with `assignTo: "page"`** to fetch the new page. `assignTo` names the reply
  `$result.page` for the rest of the chain only; two `state.set` actions then copy
  `$result.page.rows` and `$result.page.total` into `vm.rows` / `vm.total`.
- **`Pagination` emits the page as a plain number** (`$event`), while the search field and the
  select emit `{ value }` (`$event.value`).
- **`{{ vm.query }}` as a whole-string param** so the raw object (not a stringified copy) is sent
  as the JSON-RPC params.

## Page

The canonical page is [`pages/E22-data-grid.page.json`](pages/E22-data-grid.page.json); its line-by-line commented twin is
[`annotated/E22-data-grid.annotated.jsonc`](annotated/E22-data-grid.annotated.jsonc), which Storybook shows under _CDU v2 → Tables & lists_. CI keeps the two identical
once the comments are stripped, so the JSON is not repeated here.

## Expression breakdown

| Expression                | Evaluates to                               | Reactive on     |
| ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------ | --------------- |
| `{{ vm.query.q }}`        | current filter text (seeds the input)      | `vm.query.q`    |
| `{{ $event.value }}`      | the new search text / selected sort        | the fired event |
| `{{ $event }}`            | the page the pager moved to (a number)     | the fired event |
| `{{ $result.page.rows }}` | the rows of this chain's reply             | the call        |
| `{{ vm.query }}`          | the whole query object, sent as RPC params | `vm.query`      |
| `{{ vm.rows }}`           | the current page of row objects            | `vm.rows`       |
| `{{ vm.total }}`          | grand total row count for the pager        | `vm.total`      |
| `{{ vm.query.page }}`     | active page number                         | `vm.query.page` |

## What the method returns

`customer/list`, `customer/update` and `feed/list` are placeholders for your data method: `simapi.call`
calls a sim-api JSON-RPC method directly — never your Corezoid process — and a Smart Form cannot add
methods to sim-api. Use an existing method (for actors of your forms, `actor/filter/list`) or load the
data through Corezoid (`/get`, or `form.submit` with response actions).

`customer/list` receives the query descriptor and returns exactly one page plus the grand total:

```jsonc
// request  → params
{ "q": "acme", "sort": "name", "page": 2 }
// response → $result.page (assignTo:"page"), then copied into vm.rows / vm.total
{
  "rows": [
    { "id": "11", "name": "Acme", "email": "ops@acme.com", "plan": "Pro" }
  ],
  "total": 42
}
```

> Note: `assignTo` never writes the view model, and `$result` is empty again on the next event —
> whatever the page must keep is copied out with `state` actions in the same chain. Without an
> `onError`, a failed call stops the chain and the grid keeps the previous page.

## Pitfalls

- **Do not** reach for `Table` the moment you need a clickable row, a per-row button, or a status
  badge inside a cell — `Table` renders values only, with no custom cell render. Build those with
  a `for`-loop of `Row`/`Col`/`Card` instead (see E03, E23, E26).
- The grid is **server-driven**: never filter/sort `vm.rows` on the client. The client holds one
  page; the source of truth for ordering and paging is the backend.
- `state mode:"merge"` requires `patch` (never `value`); `state mode:"set"` requires `value`.
  Mixing them fails schema validation.
- Reset `page` to 1 whenever the filter or sort changes, or the user can land on an out-of-range
  page.

# E10 — Composed workspace: tabs + loops + conditionals

**Goal.** A capstone that composes the earlier foundations into one screen: a `Tabs` strip over three panels — Overview (aggregate stat cards), Accounts (the E03-style for-list), and Settings (a toggle + a conditional hint). Fully view-model-driven, renders with no backend.

## Mechanisms

- A controlled `Tabs` strip: `value` is `{{ vm.tab }}` and `onChange` writes the clicked tab's value (`$event`, a string) back to `vm.tab`. Each `TabItem` is a leaf — it renders only its tab, never a panel.
- Three panels as siblings below the strip, each gated by `if: "vm.tab = '…'"`.
- Aggregate expressions `$sum(vm.accounts.balance)` and `$count(vm.accounts)` in stat cards (Expressions §sealed/native funcs).
- `for` directive for the accounts list, with a `navigate.local` per row (as in E03).
- `state` `merge` action writing a partial patch into `vm.settings` (Client actions).
- A conditional-text `Label` reading the merged flag (`{{ … ? … : … }}`).
- `Row`/`Col` (`span`) layout for the stat grid.

## Page

The canonical page is [`pages/E10-workspace.page.json`](pages/E10-workspace.page.json); its line-by-line commented twin is
[`annotated/E10-workspace.annotated.jsonc`](annotated/E10-workspace.annotated.jsonc), which Storybook shows under _CDU v2 → Foundations_. CI keeps the two identical
once the comments are stripped, so the JSON is not repeated here.

## Expression breakdown

| Expression                                 | Evaluates to             | Reactive on           |
| ------------------------------------------ | ------------------------ | --------------------- |
| `{{ vm.tab }}` (Tabs value)                | the open tab             | `vm.tab`              |
| `vm.tab = 'overview'` (panel `if`)         | builds only that panel   | `vm.tab`              |
| `{{ $sum(vm.accounts.balance) }}`          | `1790` (sum of balances) | `vm.accounts`         |
| `{{ $count(vm.accounts) }}`                | `3`                      | `vm.accounts`         |
| `vm.accounts` (for.items)                  | the accounts array       | `vm.accounts`         |
| `{{ $acc.id }}` (nav query)                | each row id, as a string | that loop item        |
| `{{ vm.settings.compact }}` (Toggle value) | the compact flag         | `vm.settings.compact` |
| `{{ vm.settings.compact ? 'on' : 'off' }}` | `'on'` / `'off'`         | `vm.settings.compact` |

## Pitfalls

- `$sum(vm.accounts.balance)` relies on JSONata path projection — `vm.accounts.balance` yields the sequence of balances, which `$sum` folds; `vm.accounts[].balance` gives the same result (the `[]` only forces an array).
- `TabItem.value` must be unique, and `vm.tab` and each panel's `if` must use the same strings, or no panel shows. Content placed inside a `TabItem` is never rendered.
- `state.merge` patches only the listed keys of the object at `path`; it does not replace the whole object. Use `set` when you mean to overwrite. (The toggle merges the flipped value, `vm.settings.compact ? false : true`, and leaves `currency` alone.)

# E03 — List via for-loop with per-row action

**Goal.** Render one Card per account from `vm.accounts` using a `for` directive, and give each row an "Open" button that navigates locally carrying that row's id.

## Mechanisms

- `for` directive — repeats a node's subtree once per array item (TreeNode §`for`): `items`, `as`, `keyBy`.
- A plain node id (`acc`) — the renderer derives each repeat's id from `keyBy` (`acc:1`, `acc:2`). Templated ids (`acc-{{ $acc.id }}`) are refused by sim-api when a page is saved.
- Loop-scoped `$acc` variable inside the subtree (Expressions §bound `$` variables).
- `navigate.local` client action with a `query` map whose values are `{{ }}` expressions (Client actions).

## Page

The canonical page is [`pages/E03-loop-list.page.json`](pages/E03-loop-list.page.json); its line-by-line commented twin is
[`annotated/E03-loop-list.annotated.jsonc`](annotated/E03-loop-list.annotated.jsonc), which Storybook shows under _CDU v2 → Foundations_. CI keeps the two identical
once the comments are stripped, so the JSON is not repeated here.

## Expression breakdown

| Expression                  | Evaluates to              | Reactive on    |
| --------------------------- | ------------------------- | -------------- |
| `{{ $count(vm.accounts) }}` | `2`                       | `vm.accounts`  |
| `vm.accounts` (for.items)   | the accounts array        | `vm.accounts`  |
| `{{ $acc.name }}`           | row name (e.g. `Acme`)    | that loop item |
| `{{ $acc.balance }}`        | row balance (e.g. `1200`) | that loop item |
| `{{ $acc.id }}` (nav query) | the row id, as a string   | that loop item |

## Pitfalls

- `for.items` is **bare** JSONata (`"vm.accounts"`), not wrapped in `{{ }}`; wrapping is tolerated but unnecessary for `for`/`if`/`visibility`.
- The loop variable is `$acc` because `as: "acc"` — it is not `$item` here. Match the `$`-name to your `as`.
- `navigate.local` `query` values must be strings; a numeric id must be interpolated via `"{{ $acc.id }}"`, not passed as a raw number.

# R01-page-routing — Short URLs declared in a page config

**Goal.** Give a Smart Form page readable, shareable addresses — `/sf/{appKey}` and
`/sf/{appKey}/sales/main` — next to its technical URL
`/{workspaceId}/{scriptRef}/{environment}/index`, and hand the page the resolved entities through
`$route` so a `GraphEditor` opens the right graph and layer.

> **A config example, not a render payload.** Unlike `pages/E##-*.page.json`, this is a **stored page
> config** (`pages/<pageId>/config`): it has `id` (not `pageId`), no `viewModel` / `locale`, and it
> carries `routes`, which only a stored config has. Canonical file:
> [`configs/R01-page-routing.config.json`](configs/R01-page-routing.config.json); commented twin:
> [`annotated-configs/R01-page-routing.annotated.jsonc`](annotated-configs/R01-page-routing.annotated.jsonc).
> Design: [`../tasks/pretty-urls.md`](../tasks/pretty-urls.md). Storybook: _CDU v2 → Routing & URLs_.

> **Status (2026-10-01).** Everything this example relies on is merged to `develop`: the contract,
> the releases, `route/resolve` / `route/visibility` and the dynamic target (sim-api + pong-server
> migration 5.185.0), and opening `/sf/…`, `$route`, the `$route.ids` enrichment and `navigate.route`
> in the runtime. A stand that has not received it yet renders the page on its technical URL only,
> and `GraphEditor` falls back to its own `#b=` state. Full status:
> [`../tasks/pretty-urls.md`](../tasks/pretty-urls.md) «Стан реалізації».

## Mechanisms

- **`routes`** — an optional, additive top-level field of the page config. Each route has a
  Smart-Form-unique `name`, a `path` relative to `/sf/{appKey}`, and one `params` entry per
  `:param`. The page is the implicit target; no route is implicit (`"path": "/"` is declared).
- **Typed parameters** — `slug` (`[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*`), `uuid` (canonical lowercase), `int`
  (a JSON number). A `slug` may name the form of the actor it addresses:
  `"actor": { "systemForm": "Graphs" }` or `{ "formId": 1234 }`.
- **Slug = `actors.ref`** — the runtime resolves each `actor` parameter with
  `actor/by-ref/get` and exposes the UUID as `$route.ids.<param>`; a missing or invisible actor is
  NotFound.
- **`$route`** — the authoritative route context from `page/render`:
  `{ kind: "direct", params: {} }` on the technical URL,
  `{ kind: "dynamic", appKey, name, params, canonicalPath, ids }` on a short one. Injected by the
  host, like `$query`.
- **Pathname vs fragment** — the pathname picks the page and `$route`; the block's own state stays in
  `#b=graph:<graphId>%3A<layerId>` and wins over the initial props.

## Config

```jsonc
{
  "schemaVersion": "2.0", // routes are additive — no protocol bump
  "id": "index", // the page id the technical URL ends with
  "title": "Graph editor",
  "routes": [
    // The bare /sf/{appKey} opens this page — only because it is declared.
    { "name": "graph.home", "path": "/" },
    {
      "name": "graph.layer", // addressed by name, never by path
      "path": "/:graph/:layer", // /sf/k7p3xw/sales/main → graph = "sales", layer = "main"
      "params": {
        // The slugs are actors.ref of a Graphs / Layers actor → resolved into $route.ids.
        "graph": { "type": "slug", "actor": { "systemForm": "Graphs" } },
        "layer": { "type": "slug", "actor": { "systemForm": "Layers" } },
      },
    },
  ],
  "tree": {
    "id": "root",
    "type": "Stack",
    "props": { "direction": "vertical" },
    "children": [
      {
        "id": "graph", // also the key of the block's state in #b=graph:…
        "type": "GraphEditor",
        // Bind to the resolved UUIDs, not the slugs. Empty on the technical URL — the block then
        // falls back to its own #b= route.
        "props": { "actorId": "{{ $route.ids.graph }}", "layerId": "{{ $route.ids.layer }}" },
      },
    ],
  },
}
```

## Expression breakdown

| Expression               | Evaluates to                                                             | Available                        |
| ------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------- |
| `$route.kind`            | `"direct"` (technical URL) or `"dynamic"` (short URL)                    | always, once the host injects it |
| `$route.name`            | `"graph.layer"`                                                          | short URL                        |
| `$route.params.graph`    | `"sales"` — the slug, parsed by the server                               | short URL                        |
| `{{ $route.ids.graph }}` | `"d9cdcbd7-6c4c-461d-8cc2-4232b16d7a36"` — the actor id, from the client | short URL, after enrichment      |
| `{{ $route.ids.layer }}` | `"2ce71aed-13e1-4c64-b4a7-28357eb461af"`                                 | short URL, after enrichment      |

## Resolution flow

1. `/sf/K7P3XW/sales//main/?mode=compact#b=graph:…` → CloudFront's SPA fallback serves the generic
   runtime shell (200, no redirect, no form metadata). The router lowercases the `appKey` (ASCII).
2. Auth bootstrap. With no session the runtime asks the public `route/visibility { appKey }`:
   `guest: true` creates a guest session; `guest: false` or an error goes to sign-in at once (no
   guest user is created; the address, `#b=` included, is restored after sign-in).
3. `route/resolve { appKey, path }` → workspace, page `index`, route `graph.layer`,
   `canonicalPath: "/sales/main"`, `guest` — exactly one call per address.
4. Client-side workspace switch for a member (a guest stays as it is) → `page/render` with
   `target: { kind: "dynamic", appKey, path }`; the server resolves again and returns `route` +
   `routing`.
5. Enrichment: `form/system/get` (Graphs, Layers) → `actor/by-ref/get` → `$route.ids`.
6. `history.replaceState` → `/sf/k7p3xw/sales/main?mode=compact#b=graph:…` (lowercase key, query and
   hash kept). The bare root is `/sf/k7p3xw` — never with a trailing `/`.

Unknown `appKey`, no match, no access and a missing actor all end on the same `notFound` (sign-in for
a visitor without a session). Each such miss counts against the client's per-IP budget
(`shortUrls.missesPerMinute`, default 30 per minute); over it the answer is the same `notFound`
without a lookup.

## What your Corezoid process receives

The same authoritative `route` object travels to the process — in the `/send` body of every
`page/submit`, and in the `/get` body only when the page sets `meta.initViaCorezoid`:

```json
{
  "page": "index",
  "query": { "mode": "compact" },
  "route": {
    "kind": "dynamic",
    "appKey": "k7p3xw",
    "name": "graph.layer",
    "params": { "graph": "sales", "layer": "main" },
    "canonicalPath": "/sales/main"
  }
}
```

`route.ids` is client-only and never reaches the process — resolve the ref yourself if you need the
actor. On a technical URL the process receives `{ "kind": "direct", "params": {} }`.

## Pitfalls

- **Routes are not a render payload.** They live in the stored page config and are compiled by the
  release; a Corezoid `/get` cannot add or change them.
- **Slug vs id.** Binding `actorId` to `$route.params.graph` passes `"sales"` to a block that wants a
  UUID. Use `$route.ids.graph`.
- **Refs are unique per form across the workspace.** Only one layer can have ref `main`; prefer
  namespaced refs like `sales-main`. Changing a ref breaks its old links; renaming the title does not.
- **Develop never opens through `/sf`.** Short URLs resolve against the active production release
  only — save, then release.
- **Every `:param` needs a declaration and vice versa** (`route.undeclaredParam` /
  `route.unusedParam`); an `actor` lookup is only allowed on a `slug`
  (`route.invalidParamDefinition`).
- **No implicit route.** Drop `graph.home` and the bare `/sf/k7p3xw` becomes NotFound.
- **Slugs keep their case.** `/sf/k7p3xw/Sales/main` is NotFound here: `Sales` is not a valid `slug`.
  Only the `appKey` and literal segments are case-insensitive.
